articles.title: Convicted murderer escapes Tennessee prison and flees in stolen truck
articles.summary: This booking photo released by the Tennessee Department of Correction on July 24, 2025, shows Jacob Morley. - Tennessee Department of Correction/AP A 28-year-old convicted murderer serving a life sentence escaped through a Tennessee prison’s fence Sunday evening before stealing a truck and driving off — and has not yet been located, according to Tennessee authorities. Around 11:30 p.m. on October 25, staff at the Northwest Correctional Complex learned Jacob Morley was missing, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction. He had been sentenced to life in prison after being convicted of first-degree murder, aggravated burglary, tampering with evidence, evading arrest and vandalism. Security camera footage later revealed Morley “breached the perimeter fence” and left the facility wearing his prison uniform, the department said. It remains unclear how he escaped through the fence. Video obtained by the Tennessee Bureau of Investigation shows Morley stealing a white 2008 Ford F-350 with Tennessee plates around 1 a.m. on October 26, the agency said. unknown content item - The Hornbeak Fire Department , which is about 15 miles from the Northwest Correctional Complex, said it captured video of Morley passing in front of the fire department building in the stolen truck around 1:18 a.m. Morley is the second inmate to escape from the Tennessee Department of Correction’s custody in the past week. Morley was convicted of first-degree murder for the killing of Cody Birchfield, who was initially reported missing in February 2022, according to the Carter County Sheriff’s Office. Birchfield’s body was found in a box under Morley’s house weeks after he went missing, The Associated Press reported. Morley also led police on a chase that ended in North Carolina after he found deputies at his home in 2022, according to authorities. The Tennessee Bureau of Investigation, which has added Morley to its “Most Wanted” list, is offering a reward of up to $2,500 for information leading to his arrest. The Northwest Correctional Complex can house up to 1,776 male inmates, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction . CNN’s Amanda Jackson contributed to this report. articles.title: Ceasefire brokered by Melania Trump goes into effect in Russian-occupied town
articles.summary: Smoke rises from a residential neighborhood in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky in the Kherson region of Ukraine in a video the Ukrainian 34th Separate Marine Brigade released Sept. 22. (Ukrainian 34th Separate Marine Brigade / via AP) A rare humanitarian ceasefire brokered by first lady Melania Trump to save people trapped in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian town went into effect early Tuesday. After months of warnings from Ukrainian officials about an unraveling humanitarian catastrophe in the front-line town of Oleshky, in the southern Kherson region, the White House announced last week that the first lady had secured a pause in the fighting. The agreement between Ukraine and Russia would “temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway,” according to a statement released Friday. Both the Ukrainian and Russian militaries have confirmed that the ceasefire will start at 3 a.m. local time (9 p.m. ET) to ensure what they have both called a “humanitarian operation.” Neither side has indicated when the temporary truce would end. The ceasefire announcement came amid renewed pressure from President Donald Trump on his Ukrainian counterpart, Volodymyr Zelenskyy , to reach an agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war, which began when Russia ⁠invaded Ukraine in February 2022. In recent weeks, Ukraine has complained of gaps in intelligence sharing from the U.S. and a slowdown of Elon Musk’s Starlink service , which is crucial for its military. Destroyed cars on a highway from Oleshky on Sept. 30. (Ukrainian 34th Separate Marine Brigade "Borysfen" via AP) Earlier this month, Trump also eased some sanctions on the Kremlin allowing Russia to supply diesel to the global market in an apparent bid to lower prices ahead of the midterm elections , reversing years of American policy — a move that raised alarm in Ukraine and Europe. But in a rare intervention from the first lady, the White House statement quoted her as saying that Oleshky was “on the brink of disaster” and its remaining population, composed primarily of elderly residents, was in urgent need of medical attention, medicine, food and clean water. “The people of Oleshky have limited electricity, live amid mined roads, and endure regular military attacks,” she said. “It was abundantly clear that without my intervention, the possibility to bring humanitarian aid into the city and to evacuate the elderly would be impossible.” Civilian representatives from both sides will visit the town, which had a population of around 24,000 people before the war, to determine the level of assistance the remaining residents require, the statement said. An “impartial American media organization” will document the process to ensure “that the wishes of each family are faithfully respected,” it added. The ceasefire is likely to last several days as the Russian side has to “clear the roads of mines,” Zelenskyy said in an interview with Ukraine’s TSN TV channel Sunday, adding that his forces would have to verify the area is clear. “There is no doubt that Russia will do everything it can to clear the roads of mines so that these people head toward Russia and stay there. They are not going to simply let people go,” he said. Both sides blame each other for the crisis in Oleshky. Kyiv has accused Russian forces of mining nearby roads and using the remaining residents as human shields to prevent Ukraine’s army from conducting offensive operations in the town. Meanwhile, Russia has blamed Ukraine for “laying siege to the town” with drone strikes and preventing humanitarian aid from getting in. Last month, the Kremlin acknowledged problems with food and medical ​supplies getting into Oleshky, saying its military was working to resolve them. Ukrainian media has for months been featuring interviews with people who have managed to escape Oleshky and spoken to relatives of those who remain there — an estimated 2,000 people, including children. Some said the town was on the verge of starvation and residents were relying on homegrown produce to survive. Others had reportedly resorted to eating grass. With winter looming, fears of famine are growing in the town where communication is difficult because of a severely compromised internet and cellphone service in the area. The United Nations Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine, which has been documenting the crisis for months, said there have been no food deliveries to the town since the end of May. Oleshky, like a large portion of the Kherson region, has been occupied by Russian forces since the early weeks of the invasion. Drone footage of the town, shared by Ukraine’s 34th Separate Marine Brigade “Borysfen” last month and verified by NBC News, shows the charred ruins of desolate residential and administrative buildings inside the town, in a rare look at the level of destruction. Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, shared another video earlier this month, geolocated by NBC News, showing residents leaving Oleshky on foot, bicycles and mopeds in what he said was a desperate search for food. He said they faced the impossible choice of being blown up on a mine or dying from hunger. Their plight received international attention in recent weeks after Pope Leo XIV directly raised the growing crisis with Putin, and European Parliament Vice President Pina Picierno went on a hunger strike, saying “the people of Oleshky cannot be abandoned.” While both Kyiv and Moscow have unilaterally announced Easter or Christmas ceasefires before, they did not revolve around a humanitarian crisis and have not involved open mediation by the U.S., making the Oleshky ceasefire an unprecedented halting of fire between the two sides. The ceasefire could serve as a model for similar humanitarian arrangements in other areas, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Monday, especially given the “highly positive” American involvement, including the first lady. Melania Trump has been involved in the humanitarian campaign to bring back Ukrainian children taken by Russia , and the White House statement said she leveraged the “communication channel” established through those efforts to bring about a humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky. articles.title: Court rejects DOJ's emergency bid to separate Calif. ballots over noncitizen claims
articles.summary: A federal appeals court has rejected the Trump administration's late-breaking effort to force California to separate mail-in ballots from 20,000 purported noncitizens. A 2-1 ruling from a panel of the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals concluded that the Justice Department improperly circumvented a lower-court judge who had scheduled a hearing on the matter on Tuesday and moved too slowly to seek emergency relief. “[T]he United States failed to allow the district court adequate opportunity to consider its application for a Temporary Restraining Order,” the majority wrote. “The United States’s claimed emergency, at least in part, is a self-constructed one.” Judge Mark Bennett, a Trump appointee, joined Judge Gabriel Sanchez, a Biden appointee, in turning down the administration’s emergency appeal. Judge Patrick Bumatay, another Trump appointee, dissented and said he would have granted the request. Though the outcome was foreshadowed in a hearing Sunday in which the judges appeared skeptical of their power to take up the Trump administration’s case, the dissent by Bumatay created a surprising split. Bumatay said the Trump administration’s view — that a federal criminal law barring voting by noncitizens superseded California’s election procedures — would likely prevail in the end, and that every day without relief from the courts increased the likelihood that noncitizens' votes would be improperly counted in the midterm elections. “The question—does the federal government have the power to stop this potential attack on the integrity of our elections?” Bumatay wrote. “Under both federal law and the Constitution, the answer must be “yes.” Simply, the federal government has a sovereign interest in safeguarding federal elections and ensuring that the votes of noncitizens do not undermine our electoral results.” In a separate concurrence, Bennett rebutted Bumatay’s position, arguing that the Justice Department would likely fail on the substance of its lawsuit. Bennett said the Trump administration “has offered no workable plan of any kind as to how the remedy it seeks could be accomplished in practice without potential catastrophic consequences to California’s ongoing election.” California Gov. Gavin Newsom, a Democrat and 2028 presidential contender, called the ruling “a positive development and a welcome speed bump to Trump's disgusting attacks on the Constitution and our country's democracy.” “Trump is illegally trying to seize powers in the Constitution entrusted to others so he can stay in power,” Newsom said in a statement. “This lawsuit is just the latest step.” U.S. District Judge David Carter, a Clinton appointee, has scheduled a hearing on the Trump administration’s restraining order request for Tuesday afternoon in Los Angeles. The Trump administration had the opportunity to ask a larger group of 9th Circuit judges to take up the appeal, but did not do so before a deadline the court set. The appeals court formally released the case back to Carter Monday night, allowing him to proceed with his hearing as planned. The Justice Department could still file an emergency appeal with the Supreme Court or launch a new round of appeals if Carter turns down the administration’s request. A Justice Department spokesperson did not respond to a request for comment. articles.title: Trump administration attempting to prosecute former FBI Director James Comey again
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — The Trump administration is attempting to prosecute James Comey for what it calls a decade-old leak of classified information, an effort the former FBI director's lawyers immediately dismissed as legally invalid and outside the legal time limit for when the Justice Department can file a criminal indictment. The allegations from the Justice Department were revealed Monday in newly unsealed court documents that shed light on a closed-door fight that represents an unmistakable escalation in the administration's targeting of Comey, a longtime critic and foe of President Donald Trump who has faced two other criminal cases since the Republican returned to the White House last year. The effort to prosecute Comey is also part of a series of politically charged investigative actions the department has undertaken in the run-up to next week's midterm elections. “Well, they’re back — again,” Comey said in a video statement Monday. “It would almost be funny if it weren't such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice — one that we cannot become numb to. Nothing’s changed with me; I’m still innocent, I’m still not afraid of these people — and I still believe in the independent federal judiciary.” The Justice Department said it had filed what's known as a “criminal information” to extend the statute of limitations for charges in the case. "Filing a criminal information to toll the statute of limitations is a widely recognized practice in federal court and has been approved by multiple Circuit Courts of Appeals. This is an ongoing criminal investigation, and we will not comment further,” a department spokesperson said. Asked about the Comey case, Trump told reporters upon arriving back to Joint Base Andrews in Maryland late Monday following his rally in Mississippi that “I don’t know much about it. I just heard about it.” He added, “He’s a dirty cop, James Comey. But I know nothing about it.” An information can be filed without the approval of a judge or a grand jury's finding of probable cause to a court. Comey’s lawyers made clear that they intend to fight the charges as invalid because the Justice Department did not file an indictment, which must be voted on by a grand jury, inside the 10-year statute of limitations required under the law. “For the third time in little more than one year, the Department of Justice has attempted to charge Mr. Comey with a federal crime. Mr. Comey steadfastly maintains his innocence,” his attorney, Patrick Fitzgerald, said in a statement. The allegation was previously investigated The latest allegation concerns an October 2016 New York Times story related to a secret court order that required Yahoo to scan emails for messages potentially linked to a foreign terrorist organization. The story cited two government officials who spoke on the condition of anonymity about the order from a judge on the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court that Yahoo was barred from publicly disclosing. Federal authorities, including prosecutor John Durham, began investigating the disclosure in early 2017. Durham, who later investigated the FBI's conduct as it scrutinized potential ties between Russia and Trump's 2016 presidential campaign , wrote a classified memo in December 2018 recommending no criminal charges against anyone in connection with the disclosure, Comey’s attorneys said in a recent court filing. In January 2019, the U.S. Attorney’s office for the District of Columbia opened a second investigation of the same matter under the code name “Tropical Vortex.” But that investigation was closed without any charges filed in February 2020. “Both times the Government determined that no charges should be brought against anyone. Now, ten years after the article was published, the Government filed an “Information” against Mr. Comey that was not approved by a judge nor issued by a grand jury. It purports to charge Mr. Comey with crimes that he did not commit,” Fitzgerald said. Prosecutors in a newly unsealed filing said investigators found evidence that Comey “sought to correct misinformation which had appeared in the press by way of Reuters the day before” that New York Times story was published, directed his staff to speak to a journalist at the newspaper related to accuracy concerns “and thereby illegally transferred classified information.” The criminal information was filed under seal on Oct. 5, 10 years after the 2016 story was published. “But,” Comey's lawyers said, “the applicable statute of limitations explicitly demands an indictment within 10 years of the offense; an information does not suffice.” They have asked a judge to dismiss the information, a request that is still pending. Trump and Comey have a long and uneasy history The first criminal case against Comey, filed in federal court in Virginia, accused him of having lied to Congress in 2020 but was dismissed by a judge who concluded that the prosecutor who brought the charges was illegally appointed. A separate pending indictment charges the former FBI director with threatening Trump through an Instagram photo of seashells in the numerical arrangement of “86 47,” a case Comey has sought to dismiss. The prosecutions are part of a Trump retribution campaign that has even extended to Comey's daughter, Maurene, who was fired from her job as a Justice Department prosecutor in New York last year in a termination that a federal judge on Monday ruled was illegal. Comey was the FBI director when Trump took office in 2017, having been appointed by then-President Barack Obama, a Democrat, and serving before that as a senior Justice Department official in President George W. Bush’s Republican administration. But the relationship was strained from the start, including after Comey resisted a request by Trump at a private dinner to pledge his personal loyalty to the president -- an overture that so unnerved the FBI director that he documented it in a contemporaneous memorandum. Trump fired Comey in May 2017 amid an FBI investigation into potential ties between Russia and Trump’s campaign. That inquiry, later taken over by special counsel Robert Mueller, found that while Russia interfered in the 2016 election and the Trump team welcomed the help, there was insufficient evidence to prove a criminal collaboration. The two men have been bitterly at odds ever since Comey's firing. Comey in 2018 published a memoir, “A Higher Loyalty,” that painted Trump in deeply unflattering ways , likening him to a mafia don and characterizing him as “untethered to truth.” Trump, for his part, has repeatedly claimed that Comey should face charges for “treason” — an accusation Comey dismissed as “dumb lies” — and called him an “untruthful slime ball.” The Justice Department has made a series of splashy moves in recent weeks , including a criminal complaint last Friday charging two former FBI officials with lying to Congress about their participation in investigations concerning Hunter Biden, and the search by federal agents of the Washington home of Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar of Minnesota. ___ Associated Press writer Will Weissert contributed to this report. articles.title: Man charged with sending suspicious substance to 4 members of Congress
articles.summary: The case began after an anonymous online tipster told the FBI that they overheard the man talking about mailing a suspicious substance to members of Congress. (Graeme Sloan / Bloomberg via Getty) WASHINGTON — A man has been charged in Illinois with mailing four letters containing a white granular substance to members of Congress , all of which were sent in envelopes bearing his name and home address. Matthew Unglesbee has been charged with sending threatening letters containing a white granular substance to three members of Congress, along with a handwritten letter that read “HA HA.” A fourth letter with a white granular substance included the note “HAH enjoy the gift.” Unglesbee faces two charges: false information and hoaxes and mailing threatening communications. He will make an initial appearance in court Monday afternoon. A letter received by the district office of a member of Congress on Wednesday with a white granular substance spilling from the unopened envelope. The photo has been redacted for privacy. (U.S. District Court) In an interview with FBI personnel Sunday, Unglesbee is alleged to have admitted that he mailed four letters to four members of Congress after he heard about other letters mailed earlier in the month . The FBI is separately investigating letters containing suspicious substances that were sent to members of Congress and elections officials in recent weeks. Unglesbee admitted that he knew that people would perceive the letters as dangerous, the FBI said. He said in the FBI interview that the granular substance was salt, which he said “kind of looks like” anthrax, authorities said. He denied involvement with prior mailings, they said. Rep. Jan Schakowsky, D-Ill., said Monday she was “aware of reports that a suspect has been taken into custody in connection with the most recent suspicious letter sent” to her district office. The congresswoman received a second suspicious letter on Oct. 21. “I’m aware of reports that a suspect has been taken into custody in connection with the most recent suspicious letter sent to my Skokie office,” she said in a statement thanking law enforcement. “I will not let threats stand in the way of serving the people of the 9th District. My community relies on the services our office provides, and my team and I will continue doing the work I was elected to do.” A search of Unglesbee’s residence turned up a fifth unmailed and empty envelope that was addressed to a member of Congress, according to the FBI. The case began after an anonymous online tipster told the FBI that they overheard Unglesbee talking about mailing a suspicious substance to members of Congress. The tip was received on Oct. 16, and the FBI responded when the letters showed up at the offices of members of Congress three days later. articles.title: Catholic bishop says recent White House visit was 'exploited' for political purposes
articles.summary: President Donald Trump prays during a roundtable discussion at the Trump National Doral Miami resort in Miami, Florida, on Oct. 22, 2024. —Chandan Kanna—Getty Images A video of Catholic bishops praying around President Donald Trump during a meeting at the White House last week has sparked debate, with some bishops claiming their attendance was “exploited” for political purposes less than two weeks before the midterm elections . The 12 clergymen joined Trump on Thursday in the Oval Office, for what Archbishop Jeffrey Grob of Milwaukee has said was intended to be a private meeting to discuss matters such as immigration enforcement, religious worker visas, and human dignity. But in a “ public apology ” issued Sunday, Grob expressed deep regret over the meeting that he suggested was used as a "political photo opportunity” after White House officials shared images and footage of a moment of prayer. The video , which Grob claims was posted without the bishops’ consent, has been viewed over 1.8 million times on X alone. Grob said he had received “many questions” over the encounter and wanted to emphasize that the meeting “was in no way an endorsement of the President, his policies, or his party.” He said his invite to the meeting had been extended by Heritage Foundation, the think tank behind the conservative policy playbook Project 2025, and that he had been informed ahead of time there may be an opportunity to pray privately with the President. “Several photos were taken and we were ushered out [after the prayer]. Unbeknownst to the group of bishops, a video was also taken. But permission for the public distribution or posting of either the video or photos was not given by the bishops,” he claimed, insisting the bishops “should never have been put in that position by the White House.” The White House did not directly respond to questions over whether permission was obtained from the bishops prior to the video and photos being shared. Spokesperson Taylor Rogers told TIME “there has never been a greater President for Catholic Americans than President Trump, and his strong record proves it,” citing the pardoning of “pro-life activists” as one such example. https://x.com/MargoMartin47/status/2113343568823894180 Bishop William Joensen of Des Moines also issued a statement suggesting that the meeting had been ”exploited.” Acknowledging that “there are many things tied to this present [Trump] Administration that are blatantly at odds with our Catholic faith,” Joensen said he attended the gathering as the advance communication he had received “indicated that we were to have a conversation and that key officials would be interested in hearing our perspective.” “None of us bishops were unaware that our meeting was on the cusp of a national election,” he said. “Yet in no way did any of us intend by our involvement to endorse any political party or any individual candidate.” He added: “I wish I had been more shrewd and less simple, like those who exploited our meeting for partisan political purposes. I pray I am more prudent and wise going forward, even as I remain resolute in my openness to engaging and praying for political leaders at all levels.” Archbishop James Golka of Denver, who led the prayer in the Oval Office, has also addressed the matter after people raised questions over the timing of the video. “I understand that many people saw the video, posted by the Administration twelve days before an election, as an endorsement. That was never my intention,” Golka told Denver Catholic magazine . “The bishops of the United States teach that the Church cannot champion any candidate or party. I hold to that.” He continued: “I’ve had a lot of people, really good friends, ask me, ‘What were you doing?’ ‘Why did you do that?’ I just answer: ‘I was being a Catholic priest. We pray for people.'” Other clergymen in attendance included the former Archbishop of Kansas City Joseph Naumann. In a statement to TIME, his successor, Archbishop Shawn McKnight, said Naumann’s presence at the White House “was in his own individual capacity” and that “his actions and presence at that event were not on behalf of, or representative of, myself or the Archdiocese of Kansas City in Kansas.” A separate statement from Archbishop Emeritus Naumann’s office said of the event: “The bishops were assured that no photographs would be made public. They came to have a discussion on important policy matters. As Catholic bishops, they pray with everyone, but do not endorse candidates or political parties.” The U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops (USCCB), meanwhile, has distanced itself from the gathering. A spokesperson for the group told TIME that “the meeting was not organized by the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops” and emphasized it was “not affiliated” in any way. Trump described the meeting as “really good” when speaking with reporters Friday, calling the bishops a “nice group of people” who “mostly prayed” in the Oval Office. Amid the online discourse, White House Faith Office director Jenny Korn defended the gathering, describing it as “not politics,” but “policy in action ending with meaningful prayer with, and for, the President. The controversy comes as the Trump Administration seeks to maintain support among Catholic voters ahead of the midterms. According to data circulated by the Pew Research Center in 2025, 20% of U.S. adults describe themselves as Catholic. Trump's approval rating among Catholics has fallen to 30% as of October 2026, compared to the 47% he held when he returned to the White House in January 2025, per the D.C.-based think tank. When asked about the drop in support from Catholic voters in an Oct. 22 interview, Vice President J.D. Vance, a Catholic convert, said that while he believes Catholics, and Americans in general, are not “displeased with the direction” of the country, he acknowledges that “a lot more work needs to happen.” “The Catholic vote is absolutely critical in electoral politics in the United States, and particularly in the midterms,” says David Gibson, director of the Center of Religion and Culture at Fordham University. He adds that while certain religious groups may stick more with a particular political party, the “Catholic vote can shift between Republicans and Democrats much more easily than any other religious bloc.” Trump won a majority of Catholic voters in the 2024 Presidential election, taking 55% of the Catholic vote to former Vice President Kamala Harris’ 43%, according to the Pew Research Center. With Republicans attempting to retain control of both chambers of Congress amid tight races , Catholic voters could prove an important voting bloc. Yet the Administration has also faced growing tensions with Pope Leo XIV in recent months. Trump and the first American-born Pope have repeatedly clashed over policy disagreements, particularly Leo's opposition to the Administration's immigration crackdown and the Iran war . “The dynamics are shifting. For the past few years, the white Catholic vote was very solidly with the Republicans and with Trump, but Catholics are growing disaffected with him,” says Gibson. “Now you have an American Pope, from Chicago, the Midwest, and he is widely popular . American Catholics identify with him, and Trump has not ceased picking fights with the Pope, and American Catholics [could be] getting kind of fed up with it.” American Catholic leaders have raised concerns over Trump's policies In January, three Catholic Cardinals issued a “rare joint statement on the morality of U.S. foreign policy.” Archbishop of Chicago Blase Cupich, Archbishop of Washington Robert McElroy, and Archbishop of Newark Joseph Tobin said the “events in Venezuela, Ukraine, and Greenland have raised basic questions about the use of military force and the meaning of peace.” They argued that the “building of just and sustainable peace” is being “reduced to partisan categories that encourage polarization and destructive policies.” The statement bolstered remarks Pope Leo had made earlier that month, in which he warned against a “diplomacy based on force.” Trump’s war with Iran has prompted further warnings from American Catholic leaders. Archbishop of Oklahoma City Paul Coakley, who serves as president of the USCCB, earlier this year joined Pope Leo in urging Trump to pursue a negotiated settlement to the war. The Trump Administration’s immigration enforcement practices have also prompted debate. Upon returning to the White House, Trump rescinded previous government guidance that restricted immigration arrests in sensitive locations, including schools, churches, and hospitals. Immigration enforcement efforts subsequently intensified, with arrests reported outside churches, drawing backlash from religious leaders. In November 2025, the USCCB approved a special message opposing indiscriminate mass deportations by an overwhelming vote of 216 in favor and five against. The bishops also raised concerns about detention conditions, family separation, the loss of legal status, and “the lack of access to pastoral care.” The message was later echoed by other Catholic leaders across the country. In December 2025, the Catholic bishops of Wisconsin issued a statement that expressed “strong concern” over what they referred to as “the indiscriminate nature of the current federal immigration enforcement.” Gibson says that although the USCCB used to have a somewhat friendly relationship with the Republican party, particularly on the pursuit to overturn Roe v. Wade , relations have grown increasingly frayed during Trump’s return to the White House. He points to the USCCB’s argument that the Administration has denied visas for priests and bishops, and the announced cuts to the resettlement of refugees for Catholic charities. However, Catholic bishops have diverse views on politics and the Trump Administration. Last year, Bishop Robert Barron was among those selected to serve on Trump's Religious Liberty Commission. The 2025 National Study of Catholic Priests found that from a sample of 1,164 priests, 30% identified as somewhat to very liberal, 36% as moderate, and 34% as somewhat to very conservative. articles.title: Dollar General accused of overcharging shoppers in lawsuit filed by FTC and 20 states
articles.summary: By Jody Godoy Oct 26 (Reuters) - Dollar General repeatedly charged more than advertised prices even after ‌receiving tens of thousands of consumer complaints, ‌the US Federal Trade Commission and 20 states alleged in a ​lawsuit filed on Monday. Dollar General, which appeals to low-income consumers with bargain prices, made millions of dollars by failing to honor prices advertised on fliers and ‌shelves at checkout, ⁠the FTC and states allege. The discount retailer's stock was down more than 4% on ⁠Monday afternoon. "Dollar General has, for years, repeatedly mislabeled prices, overcharged consumers and failed to correct the issue ​despite extensive ​corporate knowledge of the ​problem," the FTC and ‌states said in a statement. Representatives for Dollar General did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The lawsuit cited numerous complaints from consumers, failed inspections conducted by state authorities, and undercover shopping sprees conducted ‌by the FTC. Portions of the ​lawsuit detailing the company's knowledge ​of the practices ​were largely redacted. California joined the FTC ‌lawsuit along with Florida, Illinois, ​Michigan, Ohio, North ​Carolina, Tennessee and 13 other states. Since 2019, Dollar General has paid $6 million in settlements with ​six states over ‌inaccurate pricing, according to the complaint. (Reporting by ​Katharine Jackson and Susan Heavey; Editing by Doina ​Chiacu and Bill Berkrot) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://finance.yahoo.com/news/us-20-states-sue-dollar-174735286.html

articles.title: Ramaswamy says the Acton campaign 'defamed my mother' before his attack ad
articles.summary: Republican Vivek Ramaswamy slammed opponent Democrat Amy Acton's campaign on Sunday, saying her campaign “defamed my mother” before he released a controversial attack ad earlier this month. Appearing on Fox News , Ramaswamy was asked whether he regretted releasing an attack ad that featured Acton’s estranged mother , Donna Arthur, calling her daughter a “liar.” “I'll tell you the advice I was raised in: You never start a fight, but if you find yourself in one, you finish it, and you have to stand for what is right and what is true,” he said. “They've attacked me. They've defamed my mother to media silence. It's unbelievable. And yet, at the same time, they'll trot out anything to attack a Republican.” Ramaswamy did not mention a specific instance of alleged defamation. The Hill has reached out to his campaign for clarification and comment. Acton has talked about experiencing physical and sexual abuse, along with neglect, during her childhood. Her mother stayed with her stepfather even after he was charged with sexually abusing Acton when she was 12 years old, according to court documents . Acton’s campaign in August released attacks regarding Axovant, a company Ramaswamy founded that promoted Alzheimer’s medication, and the ad's included his mother. “Today, new reporting details how billionaire Vivek Ramaswamy hired his own mother, who lacked research experience, to manipulate clinical trial data in an alleged ‘pump and dump’ pharmaceutical scheme,” the press release read. Addie Bullock, one of Acton’s communications directors, accused Ramaswamy of “shamelessly profiting off Alzheimer's patients and getting his own mother to manipulate clinical trial data, to make a buck," in a press release at that time. Axovant went public and saw its value shoot up to more than $350 million in its initial public offering before plummeting after the company reported its Alzheimer’s drug failed Phase 3 testing. An investigation by Politifact , a nonpartisan fact-checker, found that Acton’s claims concerning Ramaswamy pushing an “Alzheimer’s drug that he knew didn’t work” and making “hundreds of millions of dollars scamming people” were mostly false. New polling from Fox News showed Acton leading Ramaswamy by 2 points, although her lead is within the poll’s margin of error of 2 percentage points. Copyright 2026 Nexstar Media, Inc. articles.title: Thousands of poll watchers are preparing for an Election Day unlike any other
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — Democrats and outside watchdogs are planning a massive presence at the polls on Election Day driven by concerns that President Donald Trump will further leverage the vast resources of the federal government to interfere with a midterm that could hobble his final two years in office. They won't be the only ones there. A sprawling election protection effort on the left that is expected to deploy tens of thousands of monitors will be met by the largest-ever monitoring program by the Justice Department and still more observers from Republican-aligned groups. The result could be unlike anything seen at the polls in modern times. The effort among Democratic and nonprofit groups includes training volunteers to stand watch outside polling places and report activities they consider concerning. The network includes traditional government watchdogs such as Common Cause and the American Civil Liberties Union plus a flood of volunteers assembled by state Democratic parties, congressional leaders, national activist groups and organizations focused on protecting democracy. The Democratic National Committee's Association of State Democratic Committees created a first-of-its-kind cybersecurity unit staffed by former CIA and FBI officials to monitor and report online misinformation, including artificial intelligence deepfakes , said Jane Kleeb, vice chair of the DNC. That's as Democratic mayors, attorneys general and secretaries of state host tabletop exercises simulating worst-case scenarios, such as a surge of Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials at voting locations or the seizure of ballots and voting equipment . On Capitol Hill, Democratic leaders have assembled a legal team that rivals that of any presidential campaign. “We’ve never done this before,” Kleeb said of the party’s sweeping efforts. But “we’ve never had to deal with the president of the United States saying that he may seize ballots, put ICE agents outside polling locations and other kinds of very clear direct threats to the voting process.” The Department of Justice has already filed lawsuits in California and Alaska that could affect ballot counting or certification . While Trump continues to make baseless allegations of cheating in the election, administration and military officials have said they have no plans to deploy immigration agents or troops to polling sites. White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis blamed “radical Democrats” for creating fears about election security by refusing to enact voter ID requirements and other Republican-backed measures. “President Trump has done more than any other president to ensure we have free and fair elections,” Bis said. Tens of thousands of volunteers trained to observe State Democratic parties have trained an estimated 10,000 volunteers to observe polling places and report anything potentially concerning they might see from federal agents. Common Cause has trained roughly 16,000 more volunteers to stand watch at voting precincts, said Suzanne Almeida, vice president of states for the group. She said a broader Election Protection coalition involving 300 other groups has trained tens of thousands more. Smaller pockets of volunteers from other groups also are preparing to show up, including roughly 100 organized by Senate Democrats and hundreds more from a Democratic-allied group called Save America, which is training clergy members, veterans, teachers and other local community members. National groups such as Indivisible and MoveOn are activating their own expansive networks. There are so many organizations working to protect the voting process — including many that cannot legally coordinate with each other — that some officials involved worry about unintentionally creating chaos outside polling locations. Almeida said Election Day confusion is possible in some precincts but the nature of the threat requires a collective effort. “It will actually take all of us if some of the threats we are most worried about come to pass,” she said. Trump administration sends its own team Harmeet Dhillon, a Trump appointee who leads the Justice Department's Civil Rights Division , was asked on CBS’ “60 Minutes” whether the Republican administration is planning to send ICE agents to polling places. “There is no plan to do that,” she responded. Still, the Justice Department is planning its largest-ever election monitoring effort, with about 1,000 department staff expected to observe voting and ensure federal laws are being followed, spokesperson Kiersten Pels said. That comes after a primary season in which the department said it deployed more than 100 election monitors across hundreds of polling locations. At least one of those placements sparked tensions with local officials. Wyoming Gov. Mark Gordon, a Republican, said the behavior of two monitors during that state's primary was “a bit aggressive” and “irregular.” A Laramie County clerk said the Justice Department monitors arrived at the polls intending to interview voters, but her office didn’t allow it. The department disagrees that the monitors did anything improper, Pels said. She added that the monitors are trained to comply with federal law governing conduct at polling places and won’t “interfere with the voting process.” Democratic lawmakers and voting rights advocates have raised concerns that the Trump administration’s monitors could intimidate voters or abandon the duty they’ve had for decades to protect against civil rights violations. The department plans to send them to every state, focusing on high-population areas, jurisdictions that have had problems in the past and districts with close elections, according to a senior department official who briefed reporters on the condition of anonymity under terms set by the department. The Republican National Committee said its operation involves deploying “election integrity deputy state directors” in 22 states, among them Arizona, Michigan, Georgia and North Carolina. Those workers are the “eyes and the ears of the RNC in the field” who recruit volunteers and organize trainings, said Ally Triolo, the RNC’s election integrity communications director. Their mission is to surface anything that seems unlawful. At the same time, the RNC has enlisted nearly 22,000 poll workers and is recruiting poll-watching volunteers for competitive districts. The poll watchers will “observe the process and help ensure election rules are followed in accordance with the law,” Triolo said. Local election officials prepare for increased attention While federal monitors have quietly observed elections for decades, largely without incident, some election officials are taking precautions. Chris Swope, the city clerk in Lansing, Michigan, said he preemptively contacted law enforcement and his attorney in case federal monitors violate election law, although he expects them to abide by the rules. The Democratic Mayors Association issued guidance to local Democratic officials with detailed instructions about what to do if federal agents appear at polling locations. It notes that federal law prohibits the presence of federal immigration agents, the FBI or other investigative personnel. It also issued a reminder that federal agents are not allowed to be armed at the polls, nor are they allowed to interact with voters or handle ballots or election equipment. Justice Department officials have said their monitors won't be armed and will not interfere with voting. Asked about department monitors being sent to Georgia, Trump told a reporter recently: “They’re not going to do anything other than watch." Some of the poll observations have already begun. Mary Corcoran, Save America's executive director, said her group's volunteers have been monitoring precincts during early voting in Georgia, Michigan, North Carolina and Ohio to help give voters a sense of security. “The fear is the point, and we must do something about it,” she said. “Left unanswered, fear does the work of keeping people home without a single agent setting foot at a polling place.” ___ Associated Press writers Jacqueline GaNun in Lansing, Mich., Mary Clare Jalonick in Washington and Jessica Hill in Las Vegas contributed to this report. articles.title: Spurned by Trump, these outgoing Republicans aren't helping their potential successors
articles.summary: Republicans spurned by President Donald Trump aren't interested in rescuing their would-be replacements. Instead, a growing number of retiring or ousted GOP incumbents from Nevada to North Carolina are sitting those races out, and in some cases, openly bucking their own party. Outgoing Sen. John Cornyn has raised money for various Republican Senate candidates — just not for Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, who ousted him in the primary with support from Trump. He's been vocal for months about what he sees as Paxton's vulnerabilities and how Democrats could flip Texas blue for the first time in decades. North Carolina Sen. Thom Tillis — who has frequently criticized some of Trump's Cabinet and broken with the White House on policy — has played little role in the campaign of former RNC Chair Michael Whatley, Trump's hand-picked Senate candidate. The distance between the two Republicans is particularly notable as Whatley struggles to close the gap against Democrat Roy Cooper. Rep. Mark Amodei has repeatedly criticized, and now openly rejected voting for , the GOP nominee to replace him, David Flippo. "The bedwetting from outgoing moderate Republicans will define their legacy and only help socialists get elected," said David McIntosh, president of the Trump-aligned Club for Growth, which has endorsed Flippo and Paxton. "People like John Cornyn and Mark Amodei need to get on board and support Republican nominees and stop posturing for an MSNOW contract." But other Republicans defended their colleagues: "I never would question the loyalty to the party of Thom Tillis or John Cornyn. Both of them have contributed immensely to our party and our party's successes in the past and I suspect will be going forward," said North Dakota GOP Sen. Kevin Cramer. "But I also don't begrudge them for their opinions and their right to be open about them." These outgoing Republicans, several of whom were explicitly pushed out by Trump or persuaded to retire given his hold on the GOP, are using the midterms as a test: whether the party will demand loyalty to the president or can return to a pre-Trump era. "What [Trump's] done is created a coalition that, in my opinion, will not stay with Republicans once we go back to traditional Republican platform priorities," Tillis said in a recent interview with POLITICO . "A lot of the elements of the populism that Trump created to expand a base that made him successful running for president, I don't think that stays with the party long-term." Some of those intraparty frustrations are starting to boil over, with Trump loyalist candidates and outgoing Republicans swiping at one another as Election Day barrels closer and the party's overall fortunes look dire. The blame game is especially prominent in some of the Senate battlegrounds where Republicans have begun to quietly retreat in the final stretch of the midterms. Tillis never followed through on his offers to help Whatley by reaching out to holdout donors in the North Carolina Senate race, said one person familiar with the campaign who was granted anonymity to speak candidly about internal matters. "He was never part of our strategy because ... I mean, if he could have been helpful to us, then he could have ran," the person said, referring to Tillis' decision not to seek reelection last year. "The Tillis of the past year ain't the same guy who worked overtime to help elect Republican majorities here in NC back in 2010." One person with knowledge of Tillis and North Carolina politics, also granted anonymity to speak candidly, countered that the outgoing GOP senator "doesn't help sure winners or sure losers" and "Whatley has been a sure loser throughout 2026, running as Donald Trump's 'guy,' and making zero effort to build his own brand." "All Whatley had to do was to keep this race competitive, but instead the party is facing a potential wipeout. This is an embarrassing effort by a former RNC chairman who only has himself and his consultants to blame for the completely avoidable beat down coming on Nov. 3," the person added. Spokespeople for Tillis did not respond to a request for comment. Whatley's campaign declined to comment. Natalie Baldassarre, a spokesperson for the Republican National Committee, touted the president's endorsement record in a statement. More pointedly, she said that "Republicans who chose not to help elect other Republicans may as well be helping Democrats." The White House did not respond to a request for comment. While the dynamic is less pronounced on the House side — Reps. Don Bacon and Elise Stefanik have been helpful to the Republicans running to replace them — there's a clear exception: Amodei. Flippo, who's trying to replace him, has dealt with a host of scandals, from stolen valor accusations to carpetbagging to campaign finance issues , but Trump's endorsement helped boost him through the Republican primary in June . Top Republican outside groups, including Club for Growth, have poured millions into his race in Nevada's 2nd District to rescue a seat the president won by 14 points in 2024. Amodei said in an interview that whoever was advising Trump to jump in and endorse Flippo gave "awful advice." "The only criteria shouldn't be, 'Well, they're the Republican,'" said Amodei, who cast his ballot for a third-party candidate this week. "I mean, politics is a team sport. But when a member of the team turns out to be this way, clearly this is not a bright and shining moment for the vetting process." Asked about Club for Growth president McIntosh's criticism of moderate "bedwetting," Amodei scoffed: "At least this crowd is absolutely consistent. Forget fundamental factual and character messes that campaigns won't and can't respond to; and attempt to change the focus to party loyalty," the retiring representative said. "Let me know when Club For Growth does a statement on campaign finance compliance, stolen Valor, and individual background transparency." Even as figures like Cornyn and Amodei catch the fury of more Trump-aligned Republican forces for not falling behind the party line, that doesn't mean they're abandoning fellow Republicans overall. Cornyn has raised more than $1.1 million at events in Dallas and Houston last month for the campaigns of Sens. Susan Collins of Maine, Jon Husted of Ohio and Dan Sullivan of Alaska — as well as for the National Republican Senatorial Committee and other Senate candidates: Iowa Rep. Ashley Hinson, former Michigan Rep. Mike Rogers and former New Hampshire Sen. John Sununu, according to a person familiar with the senator's political operation who was granted anonymity to discuss private events. He still clearly and explicitly draws a line against helping Paxton, telling reporters earlier this year, "Everything I said about him in the primary is true." A spokesperson for Paxton did not respond to a request for comment. In Georgia, popular GOP Gov. Brian Kemp has been all-in on the governor's race for Republican Rick Jackson — but he's been comparatively quieter when it comes to Rep. Mike Collins' Senate campaign to oust Democrat Jon Ossoff. The governor had initially recruited, backed and supported a different candidate in the GOP primary, though he's since helped the Collins campaign with a public endorsement and by headlining a major fundraiser in Atlanta and others. Still, some Collins allies want the governor to be more involved. "Brian Kemp is someone who needs to be on the trail and someone who needs to help if Republicans are going to win," said one GOP strategist working on races in Georgia who supports Collins and was granted anonymity to discuss internal dynamics. "But he did create some of this mess with the primary he ran against Mike who we all knew would be the nominee." Meyer Sigfried, a Collins spokesperson, in a statement dismissed any suggestion that Kemp isn't fully supporting Collins: "He's been on the trail rallying Georgians to get out and vote early for Mike and Republicans up and down the ballot, and his help behind the scenes has been just as important." A representative for Kemp referred POLITICO to Collins' statement of support. Across the map, other frustrated Republicans have more directly pointed the finger at Trump for his interference, lambasting the president's tendency to prop up candidates whom they deem too weak for the role. In South Carolina, Rep. Ralph Norman said this week he has refused to campaign with Sen. Darline Graham, who defeated him in the primary with Trump's help. Graham has been under scrutiny for her lack of experience in elected office. Republicans still expect her to win in deep-red South Carolina, but they've also made late investments to shore up her campaign as Democrat Annie Andrews dominates in fundraising. Norman blamed the president , saying, "What he did to South Carolina … it's just not right," but added he will still vote for Graham. T.W. Arrighi, a spokesperson for Graham, thanked the representative for his support in a statement, before hammering other Republicans — like Norman's son, Warren Norman — who will not be voting for the GOP nominee: "It is unconscionable for anyone who claims to be a conservative in South Carolina to not vote straight ticket Republican and therefore endorse a Chuck Schumer-led Senate." In many cases, GOP lawmakers are defending their disgruntled colleagues who have decided not to help Trump-picked candidates. "Folks have to follow their conscience. If a guy 'smells bad' then I wouldn't," said Bacon, who is supporting Brinker Harding, an Omaha city councilmember, in the race to replace him in his blue-leaning Nebraska district. "I like Brinker. He's a good person."A "I believe we all ought to do all we can to help the good guys win the election," Cramer added. "But I also understand people that ... feel aggrieved and want to maybe not be as enthusiastic about that as I am." Mia McCarthy, Meredith Lee Hill and Aaron Pellish contributed to this report. articles.title: 人形机器人存储需求5年增加20倍？马斯克：荒谬，机器人存储需求“超过一切”，超级智能更是远超于此
articles.summary: Counterpoint Research预计人形机器人存储需求5年增加20倍，马斯克直接驳斥称其“荒谬”，并断言机器人RAM需求将超越地球上其他一切，而超级智能的算力需求更将远超机器人—— 这一表态，将人形机器人存储赛道的想象空间再度拉升至新的量级。 与此同时，存储芯片巨头美光科技已将人形机器人列为未来重要的存储需求驱动力，将其与自动驾驶汽车并列， 定位为“物理AI”设备的核心增量市场，并将相关需求与其现有高带宽、大容量存储产品线直接挂钩。 马斯克的表态与美光的战略布局相互呼应，共同指向一个正在成形的市场叙事： 人形机器人及其背后的超级智能，或将成为下一轮存储与算力需求的核心引擎 ，其规模可能远超当前市场预期。 马斯克：现有分析"荒谬"，机器人RAM需求将超越地球上一切 当地时间26日，@wallstengine在社交平台X上发文称，Counterpoint Research预计，到2030年，人形机器人对DRAM的需求将激增20倍。 对此，马斯克直接回应外界对人形机器人存储需求的预测分析，措辞强烈。他写道：“荒谬的分析。机器人的RAM需求将超越地球上的其他一切，因为你需要机器人在物理基底上运行，以便塑造原子。” 这一表述的核心逻辑在于： 人形机器人作为物理世界的执行主体，需要在实体环境中感知、决策并操控物质，这对实时计算和存储的需求是结构性的、持续性的，而非边际性的增量 。马斯克的言下之意是，将人形机器人存储需求仅量化为"5年增加20倍"，严重低估了这一赛道的真实体量。 更值得关注的是，马斯克进一步将超级智能（Super Intelligence，SI）单独列出，称其需求“将远超机器人”，并补充道， 约100%的超级智能算力将部署于深空计算（deep space compute） 。这一判断将存储与算力需求的终极想象空间，从地球延伸至太空基础设施层面。 美光押注人形机器人，"物理AI"成新叙事锚点 在马斯克发表上述评论的背景下，美光科技已率先在商业层面将人形机器人纳入核心战略叙事。 据雅虎财经报道，美光管理层在最新一轮AI相关评论中， 明确将人形机器人标注为未来重要的存储需求来源 ，并将其与自动驾驶汽车共同归入“物理AI设备”这一新兴品类。公司管理层将这一预期需求与其现有高带宽内存（HBM）及大容量存储产品线直接关联，强调无需开发全新产品，现有面向AI服务器和数据中心的核心产品即可覆盖人形机器人的存储需求。 这一定位的战略意义在于： 人形机器人预计将使用与数据中心及自动驾驶平台相近的服务器级DRAM和存储方案 ，这意味着美光无需大规模资本重组，即可将现有产能和技术积累复用至这一新兴终端市场。 美光当前的整体叙事已高度依赖AI与数据中心需求、DRAM和NAND供需偏紧，以及长期客户协议所支撑的高利润率现金流。 将人形机器人定位为服务器级存储的又一出口，与上述叙事高度一致，但其落地节奏仍取决于美光能否在先进制程上持续执行，并填满与大规模资本支出计划挂钩的产能。 对于投资者而言，人形机器人存储需求目前仍处于战略定位阶段，尚未在财务数据中形成可量化的贡献。 近期最关键的观察窗口是美光2027财年第一季度的业绩指引 。管理层已就该季度给出预期：营收约615亿美元，摊薄后每股收益约37.84美元。市场将密切关注，届时管理层是否会就物理AI设备——包括自动驾驶系统及早期人形机器人部署——对上述预期的具体贡献作出更新说明，以判断这一主题究竟以何种速度真正转化为收入。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: “国家队”终于来了，数据要素的老故事能讲出新结局吗？
articles.summary: 国家数据集团正式成立，沉寂多年的数据要素概念再次升温。过去几年，产权登记、资产入表、交易平台建设接连推进，行业却始终缺少足够强的经营兑现。 数据资源庞大，为何难以形成持续收入？新的国家级运营主体有望降低跨区域协调成本，AI应用则正在催生专业数据的真实购买需求。两项边际变化能否形成合力，将决定数据要素产业能否走出“建平台、做项目”的旧循环。 一、发生了什么？——数据要素再次站在政策与资本市场的交汇点 1. 国家数据集团登场：制度建设走向专业运营 10月20日，国家数据集团有限公司在河北雄安新区成立。国务院国资委代表国务院履行出资人职责，集团以数据资源开发利用为主责主业，强调央地联动、产业协同以及为人工智能提供高质量数据服务。国家级经营主体落地，使数据资源开发利用有了更明确的组织载体，也迅速点燃A股数据要素相关公司的交易热情。 这次事件的分量在于产业组织方式的变化。国家数据局负责政策与制度体系，标准化组织推动技术规则，地方数据集团和交易机构承担各自区域的建设与服务；国家数据集团加入后，跨部门、跨区域协同出现了更高层级的市场化执行者。三大运营商和两大电网参与的股东结构为网络、算力与行业场景协同提供条件。 2. 多轮政策催化之后，为什么商业化仍未爆发？ 回看行业发展的轨迹，2022年的“数据二十条”建立产权、流通、收益分配与安全治理的制度框架；2023年国家数据局成立；2024年数据资源相关会计规定实施，数据资产入表成为市场热点；随后公共数据授权运营、可信数据空间、地方数据交易场所接连推进。到2025年底，政策已将2026年定位为“数据要素价值释放年”。今年1月，行业研究已经普遍把制度闭环和AI发展视为双重催化。 九个月后，市场再次因为一家新成立的央企激活预期，反过来说明此前的商业化成果尚未充分建立投资者信心。政策和平台建设提供了必要条件，经营收入却需要客户采购、重复使用和收益分配的完整闭环。从数据资产入表到数据交易所建设，市场多次将“可供开发的资源”提前定价为“能够创造利润的业务”，结果往往是概念热度先于业绩出现。 ……

articles.title: 构建“股市+债市”稳市机制！央行新工具来了
articles.summary: 10月26日，人民银行宣布设立债市非银大额赎回互换便利（Bond Market NBFI Swap Facility，简称BNSF），用于在资管机构面临群体性流动性风险、债券市场出现系统性压力的特定情景下，支持具有系统性影响的银行理财子公司、公募基金管理人（或对应母行、证券母公司等），从央行借入央行票据用于市场回购融资，以购买本公司（或资管子公司）遭赎回公募产品的符合条件的债券或产品份额，并向央行抵押。 这是央行行长潘功胜10月19日在2026金融街论坛年会开幕式上宣布的即将出台的系列政策举措之一。彼时潘功胜指出，这项工具的目的是建立债券市场稳定机制，构成央行宏观审慎管理的一项新工具。更早以前，潘功胜在6月召开的陆家嘴论坛上也提到了“研究设立特定情景非银流动性支持宏观审慎工具”。 2024年10月，央行创设了支持资本市场的两项工具，其中的证券、基金、保险公司互换便利，通过资产互换增强机构融资和增持股票能力，有力提振了市场信心，初步建立了增强资本市场内在稳定平衡机制。此次新工具借鉴相关实践，提供了对非银机构的紧急流动性支持，与股市互换便利一起，构建了覆盖股市和债市的非银应急流动性支持机制。 防范债市集中赎回引发风险 公开数据显示，截至2025年末，银行理财产品存续规模达到33万亿元，公募基金资产净值达到38万亿元。资管机构业已成为债券市场的重要参与力量，其流动性状况与市场交易、资产定价的联系更加紧密，与市场机构的关联性、风险传染性也不断上升。 例如，2022年底，国内曾出现一轮理财“赎回潮”。彼时债市大幅调整，而银行理财也已完成净值化转型，以债券资产打底的产品净值连日下跌、破净产品激增，习惯“保本保收益”的投资者集中赎回；理财公司被迫抛售债券、赎回债基，反过来加剧债市下跌，形成负反馈循环，市场波动显著放大。 在正常市场情况下，资管产品赎回通常可以通过现金储备、资产到期回款和正常市场交易予以应对；但当多家机构同时面临较大赎回压力时，集中出售债券可能拉低市场价格，进一步影响产品净值和投资者预期，形成赎回与抛售相互强化的循环。这也是2022年底理财“赎回潮”发生的根本原因。 以往银行机构出现类似情况时，央行可以通过各期限逆回购、中期借贷便利、常备借贷便利、再贷款再贴现等工具，为其注入流动性；对于非银机构的流动性支持也有案例和经验，但总体来看，支持机制仍处于探索阶段。 应对极端情形稳定市场预期 “前期，央行就这项工具与市场做过多次沟通。”潘功胜日前曾表示，这项工具就是要在资管机构面临群体性流动性风险、债券市场出现赎回—抛售负向循环的特定情景时启用，防范金融市场体系的系统性风险。 市场人士同样对记者表示，此次工具设立的目的是在债市出现大幅波动时，阻断赎回、抛售循环，守住不发生系统性风险的底线。 “工具是在特定情景下使用，不是日常流动性供应，仅限于债市出现大幅波动、资管机构群体性流动性风险的极端情形。”该人士强调，在市场承压、正常融资和交易功能受到明显影响时，工具可以提供相应支持，为机构有序调整资产、市场恢复正常运行争取时间。但对于一般情况下，因机构自身信用状况恶化、信用债违约等产生的信用风险，仍按照市场化、法治化原则妥善处理，与工具应对流动性风险的功能定位有所区别。 该人士表示，这样的安排将日常管理与应急保障有效衔接，有助于稳定市场预期，同时保留市场主体主动管理流动性风险的动力。 坚持市场化原则，机构需承担损益 在可使用该工具的对象方面，根据公告，央行支持的是“具有系统性影响的银行理财子公司、公募基金管理人（或对应母行、证券母公司等）”。也就是说，此次工具的操作对象不仅包括资管机构，还包括资管公司的母行和母公司。 “这主要与这些母行和母公司的资金实力更雄厚、抵御风险能力更强有关，2022年理财‘赎回潮’时期也曾有母行对其理财公司提供支持的情况。”市场专家表示。 在工具的具体使用操作方面，公告显示，符合条件的机构向央行借入央票用于市场回购融资，以购买本公司（或资管子公司）遭赎回公募产品的符合条件的债券或产品份额，并向央行抵押。 上述专家对此解释，央行与相关参与机构之间是借贷的债权债务关系。机构法人提供合格债券等作押品，并实际承担损益。机构法人作为理财、基金产品的管理人（或对应母行、母公司），在紧急情况下购入产品为其提供流动性，类似于管理人跟投行为，可将公司与产品投资者利益绑定，也代表了公司对产品当时资产价值的认可，有助于有效遏制抛售、赎回自我强化。 不过，值得注意的是，相关机构购买自身产品还将坚持公允定价。市场人士指出，产品净值仍会对投资风险有真实反映，这不属于针对具体产品的刚性兑付，有助于继续巩固资管行业净值化转型和打破刚性兑付的改革成果。 避免兜底幻觉：参与机构需戴上“紧箍” 当然，并非所有的非银机构“流动性问题”都可通过这一工具解决。潘功胜此前已明确强调，工具是在系统性风险和道德风险之间做了综合权衡。 总的来看，工具在及时缓解流动性冲击的同时，也强调要维护市场纪律。央行公告中指出，参与机构应持续满足金融市场审慎管理要求，维护市场纪律。 中信证券固定收益研究团队认为，机构获得的是央票，回购融资仍须通过市场完成，基础货币与央行资产负债表规模不受影响，叠加合格抵押品与审慎要求，定位更接近宏观审慎框架下的应急缓释，而不是常态化工具投放。往后看，额度、费率与折算率等细则有望出台。 市场专家认为，相关审慎管理要求并非一次性的准入门槛，而是贯穿于工具使用全过程的持续性约束。有意愿参与的机构在平时就要体现稳健经营，获得工具支持后也需要继续保持经营稳健，确保审慎监管指标符合规定。具体的指标可以包括杠杆率、久期等一系列要求。 国际经验也体现了类似思路。英国央行的非银机构应急回购便利就要求参与者接受相应监管或取得许可，持续满足财务稳健性标准，并明确工具定价兼顾正常时期的市场约束和压力时期的使用需要。 市场人士分析，工具设计的机制是救市场而非救机构，特别是因自身经营不审慎而出问题的机构不会在救助行列。如果机构存在不审慎经营行为，在紧急情况出现时，这类非审慎机构甚至是没有资格参与工具的。在市场稳定的同时，这些个别机构依然会付出代价，以有效防范倒逼行为和道德风险。 “参与机构应持续满足金融市场审慎管理要求，是为了避免市场产生兜底幻觉，过度激进投机的‘坏孩子’也不可能得到救助，这有利于更好支持债市稳健良性运行。”上述专家称。 本文来源： 券商中国 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: AI从"朋友"变"敌人"：中金测算中国云厂商ROIC仅11.9%，对内需挤出或快于美国
articles.summary: 导读 为什么要做这样一个研究？因为 中美AI都走到一个关键节点：自己的能力撑不起自己的野心了，需要向外借钱了 ，这也是市场要“算账”、担心收不回成本，一直波动的本质。 当然，借钱不是问题，借钱却赚不到匹配回报才是问题。但 AI开始向全社会汲取资源的时候，挤出效应就会慢慢显现。那什么时候是临界点，也就是政策和经济能容忍的底线。 作为“朋友” ，AI的拉动效果主要体现在直接的投资出口，财富效应，提升效率和知识外溢三个方面。扣掉AI，美股一半的盈利没了，中国一半的增长没了。 作为“敌人” ，AI的挤出效应体现在资源品和金融资源的挤占、政策空间（美国的挤出是通过利率，因为主要依赖私人融资；中国的挤出是要通过财政与信贷投放方向）、还有就业。中国挤占可能更快，比如今年的内需。 那什么时候从“朋友”变成“敌人”？ 我们测算，美国整体能承受6%的利率和50%的价格上涨，还有点空间。中国对内需挤出更早，但非量化和长期目标函数也使容忍度更高。 7月以来，全球AI链条持续调整，背后除了不断走高的成本外，更重要的是市场担心AI能产生的回报撑不住大规模的投资，例如看似市场是在担心CoreWeave的信用风险，背后可能是担心Anthropic ARR的放缓， 所以市场要算ROIC（回报）与WACC（成本）的账 ，这与去年四季度市场担心私募信贷的“剧本”如出一辙。 因此， 决定后续AI走势的关键在于大模型的迭代和新业务模式的兑现 （如今年一季度Anthropic业绩超预期），这也恰是提升AI回报的关键。 图表：CoreWeave的CDS飙升（违约担忧）引发一轮抛售 资料来源：Bloomberg，中金公司研究部 图表：截至二季度，美国云厂商的19.9%的ROIC仍能覆盖9.6%的WACC 资料来源：FactSet，Bloomberg，中金公司研究部 除了要“努力”证明自身回报足以覆盖不断膨胀的资本开支外， 中美AI也都走到了另一个关键节点：即自己的能力（自己赚的钱，经营性现金流）撑不起自己的野心（资本开支的投资需求）了 ，需要向外部融资获取支持（自由现金流转负），而无法像此前那样只靠自己赚的钱来投资。 当然，借钱不是问题，借钱却赚不到匹配的回报才是问题。 但无论如何，当AI在中美都开始向全社会汲取资源的时候， 另一个越来越重要的问题也逐渐浮出水面：AI是否会逐渐从拉动其他经济部门的“朋友”，逐渐走向其对立面，变成挤出传统需求的“敌人”？ 换言之，K型分化的上半端能否继续对冲下半端，使整体增长依然向上？ 中美其实都面临这个问题： 近期美债利率的走高，CoreWeave风险暴露，中国内需的疲弱，都是这个问题的某种折射。 只不过，中美的传导和挤压路径不同、容忍度和临界值也各异。 搞清楚这个“临界值”，也就搞清楚了经济与政策能承受的边界，对我们判断中美的政策路径与选择投资方向都大有裨益。 一、AI走到了一个关键节点：开始从全社会汲取资源来支持其发展，中国可能快于美国 今年二季度，美国AI走到了一个关键节点： 即无法用自己赚的钱（经营性现金流）来支持越来越膨胀的资本开支，因此需要对外融资（股权或债权）来弥补资金缺口，标志性的事件即是今年二季度除微软和Meta外的主要云厂商（Hyperscaler）自由现金流都转负（经营现金流-资本开支）。 图表：美国云厂商的资本开支逼近经营性现金流 资料来源：FactSet，中金公司研究部 当然，并不是说借钱就是坏事，恰恰相反，借钱可以撬动更多资金，也可以提高ROE （ROE=利润率*周转率*杠杆）， 只有借钱却赚不回来相应的钱才是坏事 。对云厂商而言，截至二季度19.9%的ROIC完全可以覆盖9.6%的WACC，更不用说不到5~7%的企业债融资。 只不过， 当AI开始向全社会汲取资源后，我们就不能只看AI自己的回报，还要考虑由此对传统部门的挤出效应 ，加总到一起是什么效果，最终来影响政策走向与市场方向。 美国是如此，中国也是类似。 而且，由于中国的AI投资ROIC更低（截至二季度，中国头部云厂商如腾讯、阿里巴巴及百度的加权ROIC约11.9%，低于美国云厂商的19.9%），且二季度自由现金流均已转负，需要更多外部资金支持。 在非完全市场定价决定要素资源分配的环境下，对传统需求的挤出可能更快。 图表：截至二季度，中国头部云厂商的加权ROIC约11.9%，低于美国云厂商 资料来源：FactSet，中金公司研究部 图表：中国头部云厂商二季度自由现金流均已转负 资料来源： Bloomberg，中金公司研究部 二、主要经济部门划分：AI与其他部门“五五开”；美国AI生产多，中国AI基建多 界定清楚新技术的投资生产、应用和其他传统部门，是我们判断AI是传统需求的“朋友”还是“敌人”，以及一轮技术扩张是局部繁荣，还是广泛的经济增长的前提。 技术革命的经济影响，不能只观察技术生产部门。 技术革命对经济的影响既可能来自新技术本身的投资与生产，也可能来自新技术应用带来的生产率改善和新供给创造，也有可能通过要素价格影响到尚未有效采用新技术的部门。 不难理解，新技术对不同部门的影响存在明显差异。 参考Stiroh（2002）的思路，我们将经济体划分为四个部门，更好体现技术革命的影响，具体来看： 1) AI生产部门， 主要涉及AI大模型生产环节，如电子计算机、软件、数据中心/云服务、IT服务； 2) AI基建部门， 主要涉及AI数据中心的基础设施和能源环节，是AI生产直接拉动的部门，如电力、建筑、建材、金属、机械和电气设备； 3) AI应用部门， 包括金融、专业服务、研发、医药、影视传媒等； 4) 其他部门， 与AI投资和消费直接无关的部门，如食品饮料、地产、交运仓储、文娱等。 对于美国， 截至2026年上半年，相比2022，AI生产部门占比上升2.4ppt至10.3%；AI应用和基础设施部门基本持平，合计比例约40%。其他部门依然超过50%，不过相比2022年底下降1.4ppt。 简言之，AI相关与不相关部门大体五五开。 对于中国，AI相关与不相关部门大体也是五五开，不过AI相关部门的结构与美国差异明显。 截至2025年底，AI生产部门占比不到5%，仅有美国的一半；AI应用部门份额与美国相差无几；不过AI基建部门的份额接近14%，约为美国的2倍；其他部门占比约50%，和美国接近。 图表：美国AI相关与不相关部门大体五五开 资料来源：BEA，中金公司研究部 图表：中国也大体是五五开，但结构与美国差异较大，基建比例更高 资料来源：Wind，中金公司研究部 三、AI作为“朋友”，如何拉动其他部门？拉动投资出口、财富效应和提高劳动生产率 作为传统需求的朋友， AI的正外部性主要体现在直接通过投资拉动增长和出口、提升劳动生产率、以及财富效应这三个方面。 ► 直接通过投资和出口等拉动增长。 这一点在过去几个季度尤为明显，中美都是如此。二季度，美国实际GDP环比折年增长2.2%，如果扣掉进口因素，AI广义需求（AI生产投资和基建）对美国增长贡献28%，拉动约0.6ppt。同期，中国实际GDP季调环比折年4.77%，AI贡献47%。对中国的拉动主要体现在出口上，AI相关产品对净出口同比增长的贡献超过60%，净出口对GDP增长贡献21%，拉动GDP增长0.6ppt。盈利也是如此，AI相关板块贡献美股增长的53%，贡献了A股和港股19%和2.4%。 换言之，美国扣掉AI，一半的盈利没了；中国扣掉AI，一半的增长没了。 图表：二季度，美国实际GDP环比折年增长2.2%，AI相关需求贡献28%增长 资料来源：Haver，中金公司研究部 图表：二季度，中国实际GDP季调环比折年4.77%，AI相关需求贡献47%增长 资料来源：Wind，中金公司研究部 ► 市场上涨带来的财富效应。 提升劳动生产率及知识外溢带来的正外部性。AI拉动经济的第一性原理来自其相对低成本、高效率完成任务后对劳动生产率的提升。 Anthropic测算，AI辅助可使部分任务完成时间平均缩短80%，且相对劳动力成本更低。随着大模型应用场景日益丰富，美国非农部门整体劳动生产率有所提升。其中，AI投入较多的行业如信息技术、金融保险的劳动生产率改善尤为明显。生产效率的改善，一方面提升了全要素生产率，另一方面，也驱动了词元调用量持续高速增长，云厂商算力投入不断加码，AI算力、基础设施等相关环节需求快速扩张。 知识外溢带来正外部性： 模型、软件、数据和组织经验向更多企业传播，可降低后续成本，使此前AI使用强度较低的其他部门逐渐转变为应用部门。知识扩散还可能产生未被完全定价的正外部性，令AI的社会收益高于私人收益。2025年，Brynjolfsson 等（2026）估计，美国用户从生成式AI聊天工具获得的年度消费者剩余约为1162亿美元。同期Gartner预测全球终端购买者在生成式AI模型上的支出仅为142亿美元，前者约为后者的8.2倍。对照其他行业，UberX用户每支付1美元基础车费产生约1.57美元的消费者剩余，移动通信的消费者剩余为1倍，生成式AI则高达8.2倍。从结果看，AI的社会收益显著高于私人收益，因此仅以模型市场交易额衡量其经济贡献，将系统性遗漏掉最大的一块社会福利价值。 四、AI作为“敌人”，如何挤出其他部门？挤占要素资源、约束政策空间以及替代部分就业 然而， 一旦AI对社会产生的回报（自身ROIC与正外部性）小于AI对其它部门资源的挤占，AI就有可能从传统需求的“朋友”变成“敌人” 。AI开始需要外部融资和推高原材料价格，就是从要素资源对传统需求挤占的典型例子，体现在三个方面： ► 挤占实物资源。AI消耗电力等关键资源，并推高其它部门关键要素的边际成本和产能利用率。 AI资本开支并非单纯资金支出，还需要芯片、服务器、电力、电网接入、土地等实物投入。当相关供给短期缺乏弹性时，新增AI项目可能通过推高电价、设备交付价格、建设成本及高技能工资等形式，挤占其它部门的实物资源。2022年底以来，美国私营部门数据中心建造支出增长近5倍。全球数据中心耗电量占产电比例从2020年的1.0%升至2025年的1.5%，尤其是美国这一比例从2020年的2.6%快速升至2025年的4.9%。此外，过去几年随AI的发展，美国油气、电气设备、采掘、机械和电子等行业产能利用率明显抬升。今年以来，存储价格上涨110%，推动美国PPI里的电子元件及配件分项同比从去年底的4%最高升至6月的29%，为美国PPI同比抬升的主要贡献之一。 这本质上是测算经济和政策能承受的代价，比如当资源都铺向科技时，K型的上端能对冲下端多久？美联储何时停止加息、甚至转向降息？中国政策何时更多关注更弱的内需？ 在具体测算过程中，需要注意的是，中美由于AI资金来源和政策目标不同，决定了挤出路径和临界点也有差异： 1）美国AI融资绝大部分来自私人部门，因此主要通过利率和美联储政策来挤出；2）中国至少有三成来自政策相关资金，且银行信贷等也有政策导向，因此更多通过财政和信贷资源的倾斜来挤出。此外，中国更关注长期战略，因此对短期的挤出的容忍度也更高。 ► 美国能承受多高的利率？整体6%左右，AI 7%以上，传统4%左右。 美国AI和传统需求板块的投资回报相对融资成本差异显著。五大云厂商的ROIC（20%）仍远高于WACC（9%），而传统需求如利率敏感的地产，抵押贷款利率（7.5%）早已高于租金回报率（6.86%）。美股内部AI和非AI的差异同样很大，我们将标普500中信息技术与通讯服务行业加上可选消费行业中的亚马逊作为美股AI的代表，其余406只成分股作为非AI的传统需求代表。截至2026年三季度，AI板块的ROIC（35%左右）与WACC（10~15%）差值高达21%，而非AI仅为3%。 我们假设ROIC不变，若五大云厂商的ROIC与WACC之差收窄至2015-2023年AI趋势兴起之前的平均水平8ppt，对应WACC约11.9%。综合考虑美债利率上行对债券成本和股权成本的影响，假定β不变，倒算得到无风险利率约7~7.5%。 传统部门能承受利率4%左右。 1）以地产为例，假设30年抵押贷款利率与近年租金回报率（6.2%）打平，再根据抵押贷款利率（拆分为10年美债利率、MBS利差和一二级利差）分项中MBS利差和一二级利差2015年以来的均值，推算对应10年美债利率约4~4.2%。2）标普500中“非AI”板块（除信息技术、通信服务和亚马逊），假定ROIC与WACC之差回到2015年以来均值4.5%，对应WACC 9.7%，回归得到对应10年美债利率为4%。 美国整体经济能承受利率约为5.5~6%， 考虑：1）AI对美国GDP贡献约30~50%，2）标普中AI与非AI市值权重约“五五开”，加权得到美国整体经济能承受的利率约为5.5~6%。 图表：假设ROIC不变，若云厂商ROIC与WACC之差回到均值，对应的美债收益率7~7.5% 资料来源：Bloomberg，FactSet，中金公司研究部 图表：若抵押贷款利率与近年租金回报率（6.2%）打平，则对应10年美债利率在4%左右 资料来源：Bloomberg，Haver，中金公司研究部 ► 美国能承受多高的成本上升？整体50%，AI应用部门4-5%，其他部门8-10%。 AI生产投资一方面拉动上游产业链的需求，但也带动原材料和相关商品价格上涨，挤压其他部门利润。我们测算，假设云厂商资本开支达到9000亿美元，剔除进口漏出效应，如果AI相关成本涨价50%，那么资本开支带来的1617亿美元总盈利（GOS）将被成本涨价和进口漏出抵消；当成本涨价3.6%，那应用部门从资本开支获得的收益将被成本价格上涨挤出；若成本上涨8.6%，那其他部门的收益也将被抹平。AI生产、基础设施部门在成本涨价过程中整体没有明显损失，甚至部分受益。 图表：AI主要成本项变动对盈利削弱的情景假设 资料来源：BEA，中金公司研究部 ► 中国政策能承受多大的挤出？ 由于政策更多关注长期战略目标，而无法简单量化测算，因此需要从三个维度来“测算”政策的临界点： 1）增长 ，《辅导百问》指出，为实现长期增长目标，2035年实现人均国内生产总值达到中等发达国家水平； 2）就业 ，关乎社会稳定，目前尚未达到“924”政策发力前低点； 3）杠杆与资产负债表 。任何低回报的投资最终都只能转化为债务和过剩产能。不论是银行还是地方政府的债务，最终背后的信用都是中央政府。但狭义口径看，财政空间相对有限（广义赤字率已经高达8%以上，非金融部门整体的杠杆率308%，甚至高于美国的251%）。 “十五五”规划中将“加快高水平科技自立自强，引领发展新质生产力”进行专章部署，自主可控和科技创新是关键两大中长期抓手。 战略目标明确、短期压力可控、财政空间没那么大，因此财政力度和政策方向的大幅转向可能还需要一定时间或更大压力。 图表：美国AI投资由私人部门主导，但中国则是政府和私人部门的双轮驱动 资料来源：FactSet，中金公司研究部 图表：中国计算机通信和电子和通用设备制造的产能利用率分位数较高 资料来源：Wind，中金公司研究部 本文来源： Kevin策略研究 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: “72%的Token消耗却仅占27%的支出”--AI多空之争的关键议题
articles.summary: AI需求数据正在制造一场罕见的市场分歧：同一组数字，多头和空头各取所需，双方都宣称胜利。这场争论的核心，是一个令人不安的结构性矛盾—— Token消耗量爆炸式增长，但绝大多数增量流向了收费最低的模型，而服务这些Token的GPU成本却在同步攀升。 据高盛Bobby Molavi在其最新报告中披露，OpenRouter数据显示，开源权重模型（open-weight models）在9月第二周处理了72%的Token流量，却仅获得27%的平台总支出；与此同时，闭源模型虽然份额从1月初的89%降至73%，仍牢牢掌控着绝大部分货币化收益。 更值得关注的是，OpenRouter平台9月中旬约69%的Token来自中国AI实验室。Molavi将当前市场定性为“无法操作”（unplayable），并指出AI生产力红利迄今尚未在科技行业以外留下可量化的痕迹。 这一结构性矛盾正在重塑市场对AI投资回报的预期。 GPU租金持续上涨，Token售价持续下跌，两端同时承压，意味着算力供应商坐享租金红利，而为此买单的企业客户和最终股东，却面临ROI难以兑现的困境。Meta近期向股东募资最高950亿美元用于AI资本开支，其芯片供应商同步入股，标志着“供应商融资”已从债务形式演变为股权形式， 资本循环的可持续性疑问愈发迫切 。 Token需求爆炸：250倍增长背后的真实图景 需求本身的增长无可置疑。 Molavi援引OpenRouter数据指出，Token需求自去年11月以来增长了27倍，开源权重模型目前占据72%的Token份额。从更长周期看，OpenRouter平台周度Token处理量从2025年1月中旬的0.5万亿枚，飙升至9月14日当周的128.4万亿枚， 20个月内增长约250倍 。 GPU定价同样印证了需求的真实性。 H200租赁价格年内上涨160%，B200上涨120%，H100上涨35%。更具说服力的是， 2020年出产的A100芯片，其当前租赁价格已高于年初水平 ，这直接冲击了此前关于GPU折旧周期的核心假设——若一块芯片在六年后仍能产生更高收益，那么以三年为基准的悲观折旧预测便站不住脚，超大规模云厂商（hyperscaler）的长期盈利潜力也因此需要重新评估。 对多头而言，这是最有力的论据：需求是真实的，算力资产的经济寿命比空头预期的更长。 Token价格的自由落体：历史上最快的通缩 然而，需求爆炸的另一面，是Token价格以前所未有的速度崩塌。据Epoch AI于9月22日发布的研究报告《思维价格的暴跌》（The Plunging Price of Thought）， 自2023年以来，达到同等AI性能水平的成本每季度下降约47%，即每年降低约13倍；在前沿模型领域，这一速度更快，平均每季度下降66%，即每年降低约75倍。 Epoch AI给出的最直观案例： 2025年1月，OpenAI的o3模型在GPQA Diamond博士级科学题基准测试中答对75%，每题成本约0.30美元；如今GPT-5.6 Luna达到同等分数，每题成本仅0.0004美元， 18个月内价格下降725倍 ——相当于一辆标价5万美元的汽车跌价至69美元。 从历史横向比较来看，大语言模型推理价格的下降速度是DNA测序的4倍、1940至2001年间计算能力提升速度的6倍、锂离子电池的18倍、电力的54倍。 不过， 客户实际支付的价格下降远慢于标价 。YipitData追踪的近2千万亿（quadrillion）年化Token数据显示，API服务的有效Token定价在2025年下半年下降了39%（OpenRouter上为44%），但截至2026年5月的年初至今仅下降6%。 原因在于： 开发者持续追逐更便宜的模型，而企业客户则在增加高端模型的使用比例，前沿实验室凭借最新模型的溢价能力暂时支撑了收入端——但Epoch的数据表明，这种溢价的半衰期以季度计，因为开源克隆版本很快便能以极低成本完成同等任务。 多空分歧的核心：谁在赚钱，谁在买单 这正是Molavi所描述的"同一数据，两种解读"困境的核心所在。 多头的逻辑是：需求持续扩大，可寻址市场（TAM）仍在增长，Token消耗量的爆炸式增长证明AI正在被广泛采用。 空头的逻辑则是： 每Token成本在上升，每Token收入在下降，而增量流量的主体正是那些收费最低的开源模型。 OpenRouter数据清晰呈现了这一图景：开源权重模型处理了72%的Token，却只拿走27%的支出；中国AI实验室贡献了平台近七成的Token流量。高盛动量篮子（Goldman momo basket）恰好在6月底见顶，时间节点与中国开源权重模型大规模涌入AI市场高度吻合。 Molavi将这一矛盾概括为： GPU租金上涨与Token售价下跌，是同一挤压从两端呈现的结果。 对GPU持有者而言是利好；对支付租金的企业而言，则是另一番景象。 生产力红利缺席：S&P 493的沉默 AI资本开支的终极逻辑，是通过生产力提升带动全社会收益。但目前，这一逻辑尚未在科技行业以外得到数据验证。 Molavi援引一份策略师报告指出， AI“尚未在科技宇宙以外的关键数据中呈现出可量化的生产力提升” ：Mag 7（七大科技巨头）的人均营收和利润率均有所提升，但S&P 493（标普500其余493家公司）的对应指标几乎持平。 这一现实正在改变企业界的AI决策逻辑。 Molavi观察到，大量企业正从"Token支出与增长和生产力的相关性"转向"Token支出与成本及利润率影响"的审视框架。 CFO们已经找到了AI这条预算线，他们想知道花出去的钱买到了什么。 “繁荣循环”与资本可持续性之问 支撑当前AI资本开支狂潮的，是Molavi所描述的一个“繁荣循环”：超大规模云厂商的资本开支越多，流入AI生态的收入就越多，进而吸引风险资本和成长股权资本涌入，形成双向资金流——而这一切的锚点，是最初的AI资本开支本身。 这个循环的致命弱点，在于其可持续性：一旦资本开支放缓，整个生态的收入能否自我维持？ 私募市场同样未能免疫。 Molavi指出，当前的退出案例“数量可观但极度集中”（SpaceX、Cerebras、Cursor、Hugging Face），部分项目的估值重估"除了一份投资意向书之外没有任何催化剂"，整个私募市场的交易逻辑"仿佛Token时代永不落幕、万物皆将被颠覆"。 在融资端，随着债务窗口收窄，Meta近期宣布向股东募资最高950亿美元用于AI资本开支，其芯片供应商同步参与入股。 供应商融资已从债务形式演变为股权形式，提供者与使用者之间的收入与融资边界日益模糊。 Molavi将整场辩论的本质归结为四个问题： 建设成本几何、谁来买单、痛苦是否值得、以及需要等待多久才能看到收入回报。 当前的数据格局是：Token需求增长250倍，但增量收益流向收费最低的模型；GPU租金上涨，但账单最终转嫁给股东；生产力红利在科技行业以外尚无踪迹。 Molavi的结论是，需求的真实性无可置疑，但 “需求增长250倍，而资金流向最廉价模型、租金流向GPU持有者、账单转嫁给股东”，并非当初资本开支所承诺的ROI故事。 在这场多空拔河中，空头或许握有更有力的那半段绳子。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 芯片股领衔日韩股市反弹，韩国大涨4.5%，SK海力士涨逾6%
articles.summary: Anthropic递交IPO申请，重燃市场对人工智能交易的热情，推动亚太股市周二普遍走高，芯片股成为最大赢家。日经225指数涨1.7%，韩国综合股价指数（Kospi）大涨4.5%，MSCI亚太指数整体上扬1%。 日经225指数收涨1.7%，在日本市场，芯片相关股票领涨全场。东京电子涨4.5%，Screen Holdings涨5.2%，两者均受益于Anthropic上市申请所激发的AI资本开支预期。 韩国市场同步共振，SK海力士与三星电子双双走高，SK海力士涨逾6%，三星电子涨近5%，Kospi单日涨幅高达4.5%，创近期新高，凸显半导体板块在此轮AI情绪修复中的核心地位。 与此同时，美元兑日元升至157.68，较周一东京收盘价156.98进一步走高，日元阶段性走弱在一定程度上为出口板块提供了支撑。 然而，反弹能否持续仍面临多重考验。本周Alphabet、微软、亚马逊等AI重量级企业将陆续公布季度业绩，市场将密切审视其资本开支计划及投资回报信号；美联储利率决议亦将于周三落地，政策不确定性尚未消散。 Anthropic IPO申请：AI情绪的关键催化剂 此轮亚太科技股反弹的催化剂，是Anthropic递交的S-1招股说明书。这是这家专注于前沿AI模型开发的公司长期以来备受期待的上市动作，也将成为其迈向首家以AI模型开发为核心业务的上市公司的关键一步。 Anthropic的IPO申请被视为对AI行业投资者信心的重要测试。此前数周，芯片股因估值偏高及AI企业烧钱速度引发的担忧而遭遇大幅回调，市场情绪明显降温。Anthropic的上市申请为投资者提供了审视AI实际需求的新窗口。 野村资产管理首席策略师Hideyuki Ishiguro表示，"Anthropic的IPO申请预计将重新点燃市场对AI板块的兴趣。"他同时指出，鉴于半导体股估值已处于相对低位且技术面信号趋于改善，该板块具备近期反弹的基础。 与此同时，华尔街的AI融资热潮并未降温。Meta Platforms寻求募资最高950亿美元，博通安排了630亿美元的芯片采购融资交易，SpaceX则签署了约400亿美元的设备融资租赁协议。BlackRock全球固定收益首席投资官Rick Rieder在接受彭博电视采访时表示，"这是我职业生涯中见过的最令人兴奋的投资时期之一。" 韩日半导体股领涨：AI资本开支外溢效应显现 韩国Kospi指数单日涨幅高达4.5%，成为亚太市场表现最为亮眼的主要指数，SK海力士与三星电子的强劲上涨是主要驱动力。Kospi长期被视为AI交易的晴雨表，其大幅反弹直接反映了市场对全球半导体需求预期的重新定价。 日本市场同样呈现出明显的板块分化特征。东京电子与Screen Holdings的涨幅均显著超越大盘，印证了AI数据中心建设对半导体设备需求的持续拉动逻辑。日经225指数涨1.7%；东证指数涨幅相对温和，为0.6%，显示此轮上涨的结构性特征较为突出，并非全面普涨。 从亚太市场联动来看，MSCI亚太指数整体上涨1%，科技与半导体板块是主要贡献来源，区域市场情绪跟随华尔街科技股反弹同步修复。 日元走势：出口压制被暂时搁置 值得关注的是，日元在此轮反弹中并未构成明显阻力。美元兑日元周二报157.68，相对前一交易日有所走弱，这在客观上缓解了日元升值对出口企业盈利的压制预期。 然而，从更长时间维度来看，日元汇率走势仍是悬在日本出口板块头顶的一把达摩克利斯之剑。此次市场对汇率因素的暂时忽视，更多反映的是AI情绪修复带来的短期风险偏好提升，而非对汇率风险的根本性重新评估。 此外，日本交易所集团定于周二稍晚公布季度业绩，投资者正密切关注企业盈利季的进展，这也将为市场提供更多关于日本经济基本面的参考信号。 反弹可持续性：盈利季与美联储构成双重考验 尽管当日市场表现强劲，多位市场人士对反弹的持续性持审慎态度，认为本周的盈利数据与政策信号将是决定性因素。 Fibonacci Asset Management Global首席执行官Jung In Yun表示，"关键问题在于本周的业绩能否重建市场对AI相关需求持久性的信心。要使复苏得以延续，我们需要看到令人放心的盈利指引以及外资的持续买入。" 从日程来看， Alphabet与微软将于周三公布业绩，亚马逊与英特尔紧随其后于周四披露财报。市场将重点审视上述公司的AI资本开支规模及其投资回报率，以判断当前AI基础设施投入是否具备可持续性。 美联储利率决议同样于周三落地。市场目前定价显示，本次会议加息概率约为10%，但年内加息概率已升至逾70%。CIBC股票与投资组合策略主管Christopher Harvey在研报中指出，"本周有如此多公司发布业绩，通常情况下宏观因素会退居次席，但美联储会议及其可能颇为复杂的新闻发布会同样不容忽视。" 在AI融资可持续性方面，市场的隐忧并未完全消散。前沿AI实验室持续的现金消耗，以及涌入该领域的债务与股权规模不断攀升，已令部分投资者担忧相关融资的可持续性。Anthropic IPO申请所激发的乐观情绪，能否在盈利季的检验下得以延续，仍有待观察。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 从“囚徒困境”到“反身性”—主宰AI交易的市场博弈
articles.summary: 上周，AI基础设施的两条风险线索同时浮出水面：CoreWeave遭遇股债双杀，融资成本急升；Meta的巨额AI资本开支和自由现金流转负则再次引发市场对投入产出比的担忧。前者暴露了高杠杆基建公司的融资脆弱性，后者让投资者重新审视科技巨头不断加码的资本开支。 这不只是两家公司面临的压力，更指向同一个问题： 当AI建设越来越依赖外部融资，这场军备竞赛还能持续多久？ 云计算巨头们深陷一个经典的囚徒困境——谁都清楚集体过度投资的代价，却没有任何一家敢于单方面踩刹车。据路透社分析LSEG共识预测数据，微软、Alphabet、亚马逊、Meta和甲骨文五家超大规模云厂商 ，预计到2027年资本开支总额将超过其自由现金流，每新增1美元运营现金流，对应约1.57美元的新增资本开支。 这一剪刀差，正在将曾经以"轻资产"著称的科技平台，推向一种对资本市场高度依赖的新商业模式。 投资人Citrini在接受Monetary Matters播客采访时直接点出了这一转变的核心风险："在这场AI交易的前三年，情绪驱动的下跌都有一个底——因为大部分支出来自超大规模云厂商的运营现金流。但现在，越来越多的基础设施是靠着相当惊人的预期来融资的。"当融资来源从内部现金流转向股权发行和债务融资，市场情绪本身就获得了直接影响实体投资规模的能力。 如果市场情绪急转直下，那些增量资金就会枯竭—— 因为这不再是一家公司花自己的钱，而是由市场决定的。 这正是"反身性 （Reflexivity，指的是原因与结果之间存在循环的、双向的相互作用与影响 ） "风险：信心支撑融资，融资支撑投资；一旦信心转弱，资金收缩又会反过来打击投资与增长预期，形成负向循环。 AI正在重塑科技巨头，也正在重塑科技巨头自身的商业模式。驱动这场AI基建军备竞赛的逻辑或许已从 "投资推动增长"悄然滑向"信心决定投资"。 没有人敢停下来：囚徒困境的博弈结构 Cornell Capital Group的研究报告《AI囚徒困境》将这场军备竞赛的内在逻辑描述得相当清晰： 任何一家巨头，如果在AI上重注而竞争对手没有，就能获得市场主导权；如果自己不投而对手投了，则面临被淘汰的风险。因此，无论竞争对手如何选择，激进投资都是每家公司的"理性策略"。 数字印证了这一逻辑的烈度。2024年，亚马逊、Alphabet、微软、Meta和苹果五家公司合计资本开支约2270亿美元；2025年这一数字跃升至3910亿美元；管理层对2026年的指引显示总额可能突破6350亿美元。高盛预测，2025年至2027年间，超大规模云厂商的累计资本开支将达1.15万亿至1.4万亿美元——是2022年至2024年4770亿美元的逾两倍。 具体到各家公司，2026年的指引更为激进：亚马逊目标支出2000亿美元，Alphabet指引1750亿至1850亿美元，其CEO Sundar Pichai甚至表示"这个数字可能还不够"，Meta指引最高1350亿美元。 分析师Amin Mrini在其报告《7000亿美元的囚徒困境》中指出， 这五家公司合计承诺的2026年资本开支约为其合并自由现金流的3.8倍——"历史上最能产生现金的企业，正走在每产生1美元自由现金流就要花掉近4美元的轨道上，靠着创纪录的债务发行来填补缺口。" 这一困境的结构性根源在于基础设施的不可压缩性。数据中心、电力协议、专用芯片，全部需要多年的提前采购和建设周期。等到需求在收入端清晰可见，响应窗口早已关闭。Mrini写道："正是这种滞后，将预期变成了义务。" 历史的镜子：铁路、航空与光纤的宿命 Cornell Capital的报告援引了三段历史，为这场AI军备竞赛提供了令人警醒的参照系。 19世纪美国铁路热潮中，铁路股票和债券总额达106亿美元（约合今日4000亿美元），远超当时12亿美元的国债规模。铁路确实改变了美国， 但1873年恐慌后的"长期萧条"中，九成铁路公司倒闭，1893年恐慌期间四分之一的铁路里程进入破产接管。受益者是制造商、农业生产者和商人，而非铁路股东。 商业航空的故事更为直白。 过去80年间，全球航空业累计净利润约860亿美元，而仅新冠疫情三年就抹去了近1900亿美元。沃伦·巴菲特曾如此总结这一结构性困境："如果一位有远见的资本家当年在小鹰镇在场，他最好的选择是把奥维尔·莱特打下来，这样能为后来的投资者省去无数麻烦。"巴菲特本人最终在2020年以约50亿美元的亏损清仓了四家美国航空公司的持仓。 1990年代末的电信泡沫则是最直接的类比。 彼时超过5000亿美元涌入光纤电缆和无线网络，大部分靠债务融资。到2002年，超过23家主要电信公司申请破产，约2万亿美元市值灰飞烟灭，不到5%的已铺设光纤被点亮使用。然而，正是这些破产投资者留下的廉价带宽，孕育了Netflix、YouTube和整个云计算产业。 Cornell Capital的结论一针见血："变革性技术的悖论在于：公司花得越多、竞争越激烈，技术商品化就越快。 商品化对消费者是福音，对投资者的利润率却是腐蚀剂。 " 现金流的剪刀差：数据层面的压力测试 路透社对LSEG数据的分析，为上述逻辑提供了实证支撑。 甲骨文是目前压力最为显著的案例。其资本开支占运营现金流的比例，从2022财年的47%飙升至2026财年（截至今年5月）的174%——当年资本开支557亿美元，运营现金流仅320亿美元， 自由现金流已转负。 该公司股价今年以来已下跌36%，并计划通过债务和股权融资筹集450亿至500亿美元用于云基础设施扩张。 微软在最近一个财季录得358亿美元运营现金流，同期资本开支（含融资租赁）达375亿美元。亚马逊过去12个月运营现金流同比增长30%至1485亿美元，但自由现金流已降至12亿美元。 Futurum Equities首席市场策略师Shay Boloor表示："投资者低估了AI正在从根本上改变大型科技公司商业模式的程度。这些公司历史上被视为轻资产平台，因为收入增速可以远超资本需求，但AI正在将它们推向一种混合模式，软件、广告和云计算的经济性越来越依赖于庞大的实体基础设施支出。" Mrini的测算更为严峻：按当前指引速度推算资本开支至2027年，再以15%的税前投资回报率为基准，AI计算收入需要在2030年达到约2.9万亿美元，才能覆盖已部署资本的成本——这相当于当前整个云计算市场规模的三倍以上。从当前约2110亿美元的基数出发，这意味着需要连续五年维持约68%的年增长率，"在基础设施市场中没有任何先例"。 反身性：当融资结构改变了风险性质 Citrini在访谈中对这一转变的描述，是理解当前AI交易风险最为精准的框架之一。 他将AI投资的融资结构变化分为两个阶段。 第一阶段，超大规模云厂商用自身运营现金流支撑支出，这意味着无论市场情绪如何波动，只要这些公司持续投入，半导体等受益公司的基本面就有一个"底"。 "无论是关税、日元套利交易，还是我都记不清2023年9月我们在担心什么，基本面仍然在改善。" 第二阶段，也就是当下，情况已经根本不同。 Citrini直接说："现在，AI领域每一笔增量支出，几乎都来自股权融资——无论是风险投资还是公开市场——以及债务融资。这意味着，AI可以变得更有用，使用量可以持续扩张，但你可能为供应它的算力付出了过高的代价；或者，情绪可以产生更为显著的冲击——因为不像以前有基本面托底，如果市场情绪转向，那些增量资金就会枯竭，因为这不再只是一家公司在花钱，而是由市场决定的。" 这一机制的核心在于：融资来源的变化，使得市场情绪从一个外生变量，变成了一个可以直接影响投资规模的内生变量。Citrini将这一动态称为"反身性"——信心支撑融资，融资支撑投资，投资支撑收入预期，收入预期反过来支撑信心。而一旦这条链条上的任何一环出现裂缝，整个正反馈就可能逆转。 他给出了一个具体的触发情景："我认为这个周期的转折，会以一声叹息而非一声爆炸的方式到来。不会是某家公司违约引发崩盘，而是：我们把实验室的合并ARR预测从4000亿美元下调到3600亿美元，然后因为这种增长已经被充分定价，这个增量变化就会向外扩散，把整个体系拉低。" 捷文斯悖论失效：需求弹性的关键缺口 支撑AI基础设施投资的一个核心乐观假设，是"捷文斯悖论"（Jevons Paradox）——算力成本下降会刺激需求爆发，从而吸收所有新增产能。Mrini在报告中承认这一逻辑的存在，但同时指出其在AI语境下的局限：企业集成缓慢、监管约束真实存在，而效率提升主要发生在模型层，需求响应可能流向应用开发者和模型提供商，而非销售算力的基础设施层。"捷文斯悖论可以在AI作为技术层面成立，同时在AI基础设施作为商业模式层面失效。" Citrini援引了Anthropic发布的经济指数数据： 任务成本每降低10%，使用量仅增加约3%。 也许你在模型不好用的时候，token需求反而更多，因为你得一直修改。"这根本不是捷文斯悖论。"他还指出，当前AI收入增速约为每年25%至30%，而资本开支增速接近60%至70%，两者之间的缺口随每一轮指引周期而扩大。 他对"什么时候会重新看多半导体"给出了明确条件："如果我们看到付费使用量持续增长，第二阶段导数重新加速，并且能够真正通过客户现金流来支撑融资——这需要采用率真正提升，尤其是对最前沿模型的采用。" 市场已经开始区分：谁在卖算力，谁在用AI赚钱 同样是高额AI资本开支，市场对不同公司的反应已经出现分化。 Mrini观察到，Meta获得市场认可的原因，是其AI投入已经体现在广告定向和广告效果衡量的改善上，带来收入增长和利润率提升。算力在这里嵌入了具有定价能力的业务，效率提升能够直接降低服务成本。 相比之下，Google和微软仍处于投入更清晰、应用层回报尚未完全反映在利润表中的阶段。两家公司都在将AI嵌入搜索、办公软件、Android、企业协作和智能代理工具中，也都在争夺智能代理工作流的编排和协调入口。但市场短期看到的，首先仍是数据中心账单。 亚马逊和甲骨文的处境则更接近基础设施提供者。亚马逊虽然有Alexa+和自研Trainium等布局，但大部分投入仍指向按小时出售的AWS算力；甲骨文对云基础设施的依赖更高，融资压力也更显著。 差别在于，AI投入能否转化为具备定价权的产品收入，还是主要依赖出售标准化计算资源。 这也是AI交易下一阶段最关键的分界线：资本开支本身不再足以构成利好，市场需要看到收入、利润率和现金流之间更明确的传导。 路透社援引Winthrop Capital Management高级交易员Freddy Lavric的话称："未来两到三年，公司需要证明AI正在带来增量收入、扩大利润率并改善现金流。如果这些财务收益没有显现，市场将开始质疑这一轮投资是否走得太远。" AI交易的真正考验，是资本能否熬到回报兑现 AI带来的技术进步并没有消失，需求也没有凭空蒸发。超大规模云厂商继续扩大基础设施投入，恰恰说明它们相信AI将成为长期竞争力的核心。 问题在于，所有参与者都认为自己不能缺席，便可能共同制造超额供给；所有参与者都提高融资强度，市场情绪便可能从旁观者变成决定投资规模的变量。 囚徒困境解释了巨头为何持续加码：谁都害怕落后。 反身性则解释了市场为何变得脆弱：当内部现金流无法覆盖新增投入，股价、债券、融资意愿与资本开支会开始相互影响。乐观时，这套机制能放大扩张；一旦收入兑现速度低于预期，它同样会放大收缩。 AI基础设施最终会成为高回报资产，还是一台昂贵的商品化跑步机，取决于一个朴素却极难回答的问题：需求增长能否跑赢算力价格下降，以及这种答案能否在今天投入的设备完成折旧之前得到证明。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: Anthropic IPO文件意外成为光学股反弹催化剂，Lumentum大涨8.2%领涨标普
articles.summary: Anthropic提交IPO招股文件，意外点燃光学板块的强劲反弹。 周一，Lumentum Holdings股价大涨8.2%，领涨标普500指数，Coherent上涨5.8%，Ciena攀升4.9%。 三重利好叠加——AI资本开支数据验证、潜在供应链保护政策预期，以及关键半导体材料供应趋紧信号——共同推动此前遭受抛售的光学板块强势回升。 Anthropic的IPO招股文件于周一正式提交，其财务数据整体提振了芯片及相关硬件板块情绪。 据MarketWatch报道，Evercore ISI分析师Amit Daryanani指出，上周光学板块遭遇大幅抛售后，市场对该板块的兴趣正在重燃，而许多投资者此前一直在等待Anthropic发布S-1文件，将其视为重新入场的信号。 与此同时， AI行业基本面数据持续释放积极信号。 Meta Platforms宣布股权融资计划，SpaceX承诺为芯片及其他AI硬件提供400亿美元融资，Daryanani表示，这些动态向市场传递了AI投资"持续韧性"的明确信号。此外，美国联邦通信委员会（FCC）可能于明年初限制特定光模块进口的预期，以及亚洲市场传出的关键半导体材料供应放缓消息，进一步强化了本土光学厂商的投资逻辑。 Anthropic财务数据验证AI资本开支，投资者信心回升 Anthropic IPO文件的发布，为市场提供了审视AI基础设施投资规模的重要窗口。据报道，Daryanani表示，当前AI行业的盈利表现从基本面角度来看"相对健康"，Anthropic的财务数据整体对芯片股形成提振。 Meta的股权融资公告与SpaceX高达400亿美元的AI硬件融资承诺，进一步印证了科技巨头在AI基础设施上的持续高强度投入。 这一系列信号共同向市场表明，AI资本开支周期尚未见顶，光学互联作为数据中心核心基础设施的需求逻辑依然成立。 FCC潜在限制政策重塑供应链格局，本土厂商有望受益 报道称，Daryanani特别点出FCC政策预期对光学板块的结构性影响。据其援引业内专家观点， FCC预计将于明年初限制特定外国供应商的光模块进口，此举将实际上把相关供应商排除在美国下一代3.2T光模块市场之外。 这一政策预期的影响不容小觑——目前全球约三分之二的此类元器件由特定地区供应商生产。若限制措施落地，短期内将对AI基础设施部署形成一定挑战，但与此同时， 美国本土制造商及盟友供应商将直接受益于由此产生的市场空间 ，Lumentum、Coherent等企业有望承接相应订单转移。 InP供应增长放缓，产能瓶颈支撑价格与需求预期 来自亚洲的周末消息同样成为周一行情的重要驱动因素。据Daryanani介绍，磷化铟（InP）这一关键半导体材料的供应增长出现放缓迹象， 表明部分供应商在提升能够满足当前速度要求的InP产能方面正面临挑战。 这一供应端约束的背景在于，AI的快速发展已从根本上改变了光学行业的技术迭代节奏。Daryanani指出，传统光学周期通常长达五年，但AI的兴起已推动"通道速率近乎每年提升一次"——即数据传输速率的跃升频率大幅加快。 更快的通道速率叠加AI数据中心所需互联数量的持续增长，将持续驱动光学器件需求。 数据中心连接需求的扩张同样将带动激光器需求上升，包括基于InP的产品。与此同时，扩大产能与产品认证均需要时间，供给端的释放将相对滞后，这意味着供应将在较长时间内保持紧张。 Daryanani总结认为，上述多重动态“共同支撑了对能够扩充产能、并以所需速率交付产品的供应商的持续需求”，Lumentum、Coherent等具备相应能力的本土厂商有望在这一周期中持续受益。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 韩国的反击：海力士额外股东回报，50-60万亿够拯救市场吗？
articles.summary: SK海力士将于10月28日同步披露50万亿至60万亿韩元追加股东回报，叠加已完成的40万亿回购注销，全年达90万亿至100万亿韩元，约为去年七倍，创韩国上市公司纪录。 但恐怕这不足以扭转中长期下跌的趋势。40万亿回购已执行完毕，真正的边际买盘只有追加部分中的回购；若以特别股息为主，它改善的是股东钱包，不是市场供需。韩国股市十月失去的“最后买家”，正是到期退场的回购盘。50万亿至60万亿够止血，不够反转——反转需要美联储停止加息、四季度HBM4按长协价出货、外资卖压衰竭三者同时成立。

articles.title: 盐津铺子三季度净利1.54亿元，魔芋之外加码海味零食与蛋制品
articles.summary: 收入小幅回落，毛利率下降、销售费用增加，拉低了盐津铺子的三季度利润。 10月26日晚，盐津铺子披露2026年三季报。第三季度，公司实现营业收入14.61亿元，同比下降1.70%；归母净利润1.54亿元，同比下降33.77%；扣非净利润1.33亿元，同比下降39.28%。 单季表现改变了前三季度的利润走势。前九个月，公司营收45.31亿元，同比增长2.36%；归母净利润5.79亿元，同比下降4.26%。相比之下，上半年归母净利润仍增长14.10%。第三季度的回落，使累计利润由增转降。 压力主要体现在每一笔收入能够留下的利润减少。根据三季报与半年报测算，公司第三季度毛利率约29.39%，较去年同期下降2.24个百分点；按归母净利润计算的净利率约10.51%，同比下降约5.09个百分点。 同期，销售费用约1.75亿元，同比增长37.23%，占收入的比重由约8.59%升至12%。毛利减少，销售端投入却继续增加，两项变化叠加，解释了利润降幅为何明显大于收入降幅。 这些投入背后，是盐津铺子正在推进的产品和渠道调整。公司9月在业绩说明会上曾表示，二季度销售费用率回升与品牌及促销推广投入加大有关。进入三季度，销售费用增长进一步加快，而收入尚未同步扩大。 渠道变化在上半年已经体现，线下收入约27.79亿元，同比增长约17%；线上电商收入约2.91亿元，同比下降49.26%。线下增长与线上收缩并存，压低了整体收入增速，也让公司的经营重心进一步向线下倾斜。 对于电商收缩，公司9月解释称，主动减少了贴牌、非重点及低毛利产品，强化线上渠道的品牌传播和新品孵化功能。 同时，传统流通渠道向大经销商集中，希望以魔芋产品带动更多品类进入终端。这套调整着眼于核心产品的销售和盈利，但三季度总收入仍小幅下降，调整效果还需要后续销售表现来检验。 产品端仍有增长支撑。上半年，海味零食和健康蛋制品收入分别增长55.68%和51.23%，魔芋零食收入8.80亿元，同比增长11.28%。相比之下，烘焙薯类、果干果冻收入有所下降，品类之间的表现并不一致。 公司也在补充新品。9月的业绩说明会上，盐津铺子披露，与伊利联名的纯牛乳无边吐司已进入零食很忙、赵一鸣门店，并推进辣味魔芋新口味产品。新品通过已有渠道销售，能否扩大单店销售、摊薄推广投入，将直接影响后续盈利表现。 现金流提供了一定缓冲。前三季度，公司经营活动现金流净额约9亿元，同比增长45.33%，主要来自购买商品支付的现金减少；期末存货较年初下降18.49%。这部分改善主要发生在采购和库存端，销售商品、提供劳务收到的现金约49.22亿元，仍与去年同期基本持平。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
